articles.title: This Self-Charging Toothbrush Has Bristles That Generate Electricity to Help Kill Bacteria That Cause Cavities and Gum Disease

paras.en: Researchers in China have reinvented a familiar tool: the toothbrush.

Brushing your teeth is an important part of your oral care routine. Both regular and electric toothbrushes rely on physically scrubbing away bacteria that can cause cavities and gum disease. But a new design, described November 4 in the journal Science Advances, features bristles that generate bacteria-killing electricity when they bend, perhaps providing a long-awaited update to the hygiene tool.

“Toothbrushes have undergone no substantive improvements beyond their mechanical function for about 1118 years to date,” the researchers write in the study. “Conventional toothbrushes often fail to establish an antibacterial environment on the tooth surface, allowing bacteria to recover and recolonize. Here, we developed an innovative self-charged toothbrush that integrates daily tooth brushing with piezoelectric functionality.”

Piezoelectric materials generate electricity when put under mechanical stress, like being squeezed or compressed. In the new study, researchers applied this property to the toothbrush by creating bristles from polyvinylidene fluoride, a material that produces an electrical charge when it bends.

The electricity doesn’t directly zap oral bacteria, however. Instead, the charge creates highly unstable molecules called reactive oxygen species in the saliva. These molecules disrupt the membranes of bacteria in dental plaque—a sticky layer of the harmful organisms, along with food particles and spit.

“The concept is great,” Nicholas Jakubovics, an oral microbiologist at Newcastle University in England who did not participate in the research, tells New Scientist’s Christa Lesté-Lasserre. “Basically, the mechanical forces recharge the surface, so it’s really innovative. Anything that even slightly improves the way dental care works could have a benefit, because oral disease is just so widespread.” Experts estimate that almost 3.7 billion people worldwide have oral diseases, such as gum disease and tooth decay.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The researchers first conducted lab tests of the piezoelectric toothbrush using two key oral pathogens: Streptococcus mutans, which causes cavities, and Porphyromonas gingivalis, which causes gum disease. The charge-producing bristles killed about half of the cavity-causing bacteria and more than half of the gum disease agent present, while traditional nylon bristles eliminated only about 9 percent and 8 percent, respectively.

Then, they moved to a human trial. The team enrolled 115 participants with tooth decay or mild gum disease, called gingivitis. They asked some people to use the electricity-generating toothbrushes and others to use nylon-bristled brushes twice a day for three months.
At the end of the study period, participants who brushed with the experimental tool had less plaque, gum inflammation and bleeding than regular toothbrush users, the team found.

“It’s great to have new approaches that actually enhance the effect of mechanical cleaning,” Jakubovics tells Live Science’s Isha Ishtiaq. “The idea that the toothbrush surface itself is actively doing something is really interesting.”
One of the limits of the research, however, is the clinical trial’s short duration, he notes. “We would want to make sure that it is safe on the tissues for long-term use.”

Frank Scannapieco, a periodontist and microbiologist at the University of Buffalo who did not participate in the study, agrees that more research is necessary to prove the toothbrush is safe and effective, per Nature’s Elizabeth Gibney.

This isn’t the first time researchers have taken a swing at upgrading toothbrushes. Previous designs have included bristles with antibacterial chemicals, but researchers aren’t sure if they have a lasting effect. Others produced charged particles to help clean teeth, but these require batteries.
“The toothbrush is humanity’s mightiest soldier in the battle against dental plaque,” according to a statement. The researchers behind the new study “have now upgraded this warrior.”
Still, there’s a long way to go before this upgrade can sit on pharmacies’ oral health shelves.

articles.title: Have Archaeologists Finally Pieced Together the 'Parthenon Puzzle,' One of Ancient Greece's Greatest Mysteries?

paras.en: When the Parthenon was built some 2,500 years ago atop the Acropolis of Athens, one of the temple’s facades stood out for its striking imagery. Stretching for nearly 100 feet above the building’s eastern entrance, the marble-carved pediment depicted Athena being birthed from the head of a nearly 13-foot-tall Zeus; they were flanked on either side by 37 other intricately sculpted figures, including gods and goddesses. For its fine craftsmanship and potent symbolism, the pediment is widely considered by scholars to be one of antiquity’s most famous images.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: But no one alive today has ever looked upon the scene in its original glory. Sometime between the fifth century C.E. and 1670, the pediment was largely destroyed—fires, earthquakes and humans all played roles in its destruction. Only 20 percent of the ruins were recovered, and these fragments have since been scattered to museums across the world. Piecing together what the original artwork may have looked like has intrigued historians for centuries. Now, a team of researchers believe they have finally reached a solution to the Parthenon puzzle.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Open this week at the Liebieghaus Sculpture Collection in Frankfurt, Germany, “Athena, the Stage is Yours: The Parthenon Puzzle” offers visitors a chance to see what the institution is calling the first-ever “archaeologically grounded proposal” for what the pediment once looked like.

“For around 200 years, archaeological research has sought to reconstruct the lost overall appearance of the Parthenon’s east pediment,” Philipp Demandt, the museum’s director, says in a statement. “With this exhibition, we are presenting our findings to the public for the first time and inviting visitors to take a fresh look at and discuss one of the most significant works of art from antiquity.”

Recreating the image took decades of dedicated research. The museum’s effort was led by Vinzenz Brinkmann and his wife, Ulrike Koch-Brinkmann, who are both archaeologists. They began by referencing the most complete, existing body of work about the pediment. In the early 20th century, Arthur Hamilton Smith, a curator at the British Museum, produced plaster casts of more than 200 small surviving fragments from the pediment and meticulously documented their known placements in relation to each other.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The duo created digital renderings of these pieces, which still left massive gaps in the overall pediment. They then began scouring archives around the world for unidentified clues to the original design. A breakthrough came during a trip to the Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg, Russia, in 2014. There, they observed an ancient Roman sarcophagus with a relief on its lid depicting the birth of Athena. The scene resembled nearly exactly what scholars envisioned of the pediment.

Brinkmann and Koch-Brinkmann are also noted for their painstaking work to accurately recreate the original color schemes of classical white marble statues. For authenticity, they used the same mineral and organic pigments available to the ancients.

“It was really a chance discovery,” Brinkmann tells the Art Newspaper’s Catherine Hickley. “We noticed a figural relief on the lid of a sarcophagus that was clearly closely related to the composition of the east pediment. It refers to the few surviving figures from the corners of the pediment, such as Helios and Selene with their chariots, but also to figures that have repeatedly been proposed as having belonged to the east pediment, such as the Horae [and] Moirai.”
Brinkmann’s team studied nine sarcophagi in total, mostly in the Vatican Museum and elsewhere in Rome. “The Romans copied everything the Greeks did,” he explains to the Art Newspaper.

While no single sarcophagus showed the entire 39-figure scene, they each showed different aspects of the pediment, which the researchers were able to piece together digitally, with the help of 3D scanners. Earlier scholars noticed this connection between sarcophagi lids and the pediment, Brinkmann tells Deutsche Welle’s Katharina Abel. “But we really seized on the idea and never let go.”

The researchers searched for missing artifacts that could piece together the lost scene. On the surviving fragments they studied drill holes and the edges of broken shards for clues about adjacent pieces. They referenced ancient texts for possible descriptions of the pediment’s positioning. They identified lost sculptures and worked with international institutions to ask and answer new questions as they arose.
“Piece by piece, the puzzle came together to form a new, archaeologically grounded overall picture of the Parthenon’s east pediment,” Brinkmann says in the statement.

Inside the exhibit, the reconstructed pediment is presented as a 13 foot-long, 3D-printed model, at a scale of 1:7.7 compared to the original. There are also life-size reproductions of the largely missing central figures, Zeus, Athena and Hera, based on surviving fragments and comparable sculptures. Casts of the well-preserved figures at opposite ends of the pediment—Helios, the sun god, and Selene, the moon goddess—mark the passing of time from day to night. A colorful animation created especially for the exhibition brings the tale to life through a retelling of the myth of Athena’s birth.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “Research belongs in the public sphere. In particular, a museum can demonstrate how scientific knowledge is generated by interpreting traces, asking questions and correlating different sources,” Ina Hartwig, who heads the city of Frankfurt’s Department of Culture and Science, says in a statement. “The exhibition makes this process immediately comprehensible to visitors.”
“Athena, the Stage is Yours: The Parthenon Puzzle” is on view at the Liebieghaus Sculpture Collection in Frankfurt through July 25, 2027.

articles.title: The NIH Has Decided to Move Its Last Group of Retired Research Chimpanzees to an Animal Sanctuary Next Year

paras.en: Roughly three dozen chimpanzees currently live at the Keeling Center for Comparative Medicine and Research in Bastrop, Texas. They used to serve as subjects in scientific studies. Next year, however, these primates—the last federally owned chimps at an American research facility—will move to a retirement home at an animal sanctuary, according to an announcement by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) on November 18.

“Completing their transfers will fulfill NIH’s commitment, announced in November 2015, to retire all NIH-owned chimpanzees to sanctuary,” says Jay Bhattacharya, director of the agency, in the statement.

The move has been a long time in the making. In 2000, the Chimpanzee Health Improvement Maintenance Protection (CHIMP) Act established a national sanctuary system for chimps no longer needed for federal biomedical research. Then, in 2015, the NIH announced it would end its funding and support of all research on the primate species. The agency committed to retire all its approximately 300 chimps and move them to Chimp Haven, a 200-acre federal sanctuary in Keithville, Louisiana.

But the plan proceeded slowly. In 2019, the NIH veterinary panel determined that the 44 federally owned chimpanzees at the Alamogordo Primate Facility in New Mexico were too old or ill to move. Many of the retirees were near the upper end of their life expectancy in captivity and had severe health problems like heart disease. Two years later, the agency decided the same for the 51 primates at the Keeling Center and the 11 at the Southwest National Primate Research Center in San Antonio, Texas.

However, in 2024, staffing changes at Alamogordo and public pressure—including a lawsuit filed by animal welfare organizations—forced the NIH to shift its plans for the remaining chimps at the facility. They finally moved to Chimp Haven last year, meaning only the Keeling Center chimps remained at an NIH facility, given that the Southwest National Primate Research Center stopped receiving funding from the agency.

Although one elderly Alamogordo chimp died on the way to the sanctuary, the transfer prompted NIH leadership to revisit the potential transfer of Keeling Center animals, Bhattacharya says in the statement. “After careful analysis and internal consultations, NIH leadership decided to proceed.”
Animal advocacy organizations have welcomed the news.

“This has been a long road and something that many people thought would never happen,” says Kathleen Conlee, vice president of animal research issues at the Humane World for Animals, to Emily Anthes at the New York Times. “It’s a really historic moment. This will be the end of the government’s use and confinement of chimps in labs.”
Biomedical research groups, on the other hand, oppose the transfer. They argue that the aging chimps would be safer staying at a place with staff they know, reports David Grimm at Science.

“These are sensitive and intelligent beings with complex social histories that include strong relationships with their chimp and human families,” says Cindy Buckmaster, former chair of Americans for Medical Progress, an advocacy organization that supports humane animal research, to Science.

At the Keeling Center, chimps have access to large, open enclosures, she says. “They have everything they need where they are. We should leave them be and let them live the rest of their lives in peace.”

Staff at Chimp Haven, for their part, are excited to welcome the animals. The primates from Alamogordo appear to be acclimating well, says Rana Smith, the sanctuary’s president and CEO, to the Times. They hope to receive all the Keeling Center chimps by the end of next year, with some transfers beginning in January.
“When that very last chimp arrives from the Keeling Center, I think that is a milestone moment,” Smith says. “We’re just happy to be a part of it and provide the chimps with their happy ending.”

articles.title: Google Built a Giant ‘Mirror Dimension’ Internet to Test Its Chrome AI Agents
articles.author: Lily Hay Newman

paras.en: As the Google Chrome team has worked to develop AI browsing features using the company's Gemini models, they realized they need to go the extra mile to keep things from going haywire. So they did the only thing they could think to do—they built an expansive alternate-universe internet that they completely control.

“Web-use” agents need to be familiar with the open internet, how to navigate real websites and platforms, and how to be hardened against web attacks. So training them in limited test environments is only so effective. Plus, models can develop what's known as “eval awareness” where they behave differently because they have determined that they are in a test or simulation. On the other hand, setting unrefined agents loose on the open internet is a bad idea. That’s where the alternate-universe internet comes in.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The “Mirror Dimension,” which Google is detailing in a blog post today for the first time, is a sweeping and diverse but isolated web ecosystem that the Chrome team entirely controls. It includes a vast array of websites and platforms—including social media sites, shopping, and bank dashboards—that are built with all the components and attributes of real websites. Browsing assistant agents must interact with the sites and complete tasks in Chrome the way they would on the real internet. And they face resilience tests as they go, like hidden prompt-injection attacks, to test their defenses.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “Agents are not programmed so you can’t predict every possible thing an agent might see, the exploration space that we have to address is huge and the web is hostile,” says Charles Qian, a software engineer on the Chrome AI security team. “Any user can ask any prompt on any website, so we really need to explore that space as thoroughly as we can. And we’ve seen the agent start to develop a mature sense of judgement when it comes to knowing what information is actually needed for a task and when to punt back to the user for a confirmation.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Building out and populating the Mirror Dimension was a challenge in itself, because it needed to be vast and varied enough to represent the scale of the real web while being developed quickly. To construct it, the Chrome team gathered armies of website and web app development agents guided by a purpose-built AI harness to quickly create realistic web services and data flows—down to details like entering promo codes on a shopping site or populating social media pages.

Even though the entire environment is controlled by Google, Chrome is built with so many user protections and validity checks that in order to allow the agents to use real Chrome (which is crucial for accurate training), the researchers essentially had to hack the browser and take elaborate steps like making forged web certificates for validity checks so the agents could have a normal experience. The team emphasizes, though, that none of these attacks would be possible against regular Chrome users on the open internet. They were all facilitated by the god-mode type access and privilege the team inherently has because they control the entire environment and network.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The researchers say that while the browsing assistant agents they have been testing are benign and do not have cyber capabilities, their goal is to make the Mirror Dimension available to teams across Google so more researchers have access to the safe and controlled environment for testing.

“We’re sharing this approach so other teams both internally and externally think about doing it this way,” says Doug Turner, Google’s director of engineering. “This is the first step, there’s going to be continued investment in this approach to train models. And I would imagine as they become more sophisticated we’ll have to continue working on this environment to make it more and more realistic.”

articles.title: The Jensen Huang Blast Radius Has Hit His Favorite Restaurants
articles.author: Amy Chang Chien

paras.en: Few things could generate more buzz for a small restaurant than a visit from Jensen Huang. In recent years, the former Nvidia CEO became known for dining out at street markets and hole-in-the-wall noodle joints across Asia, drawing huge crowds of fans and photographers wherever he went.
paras.zh: 对于一家小餐馆来说，很少有事情能比黄仁勋的到访更能引起轰动。近年来，这位前英伟达首席执行官因在亚洲各地街头市场和小面馆用餐而闻名，无论他走到哪里，都会吸引大批粉丝和摄影师。

paras.en: But after Huang resigned last week amid revelations of multiple extramarital affairs, some of the food vendors he helped put on the map are wondering whether their most famous customer is still good for business. In Taiwan, where Huang was born and his dining habits have long been a spectator sport, many say they aren't ready to turn against their hometown hero.
paras.zh: 但在上周黄仁勋因多起婚外情被曝光而辞职后，他曾帮助打响名气的一些餐饮商家开始怀疑，这位最著名的顾客是否还能为他们的生意带来好处。在黄仁勋的出生地台湾，他的饮食习惯早已成为人们津津乐道的话题。许多人表示，他们还没有准备好背弃这位家乡英雄。

paras.en: Tu Chang-chun, the owner of Ice World, a shaved-ice shop in Taipei, describes Huang as friendly, the kind of person who puts others around him at ease. His impression of the billionaire hasn’t changed since he learned of his affair with Alice Huang, a businesswoman accused of spying for China.
paras.zh: 台北刨冰店“冰世界”的老板涂长春形容黄仁勋为人友善，是那种能让周围人感到放松的人。自从他得知这位亿万富翁与被指控为中国从事间谍活动的女商人黄雪琴有染以来，他对他的印象一直没有改变。

paras.en: “It’s not as if he killed someone or set something on fire. Why blow it all out of proportion?” Tu said on Monday evening, standing beneath the yellow lights of his stall at Linjiang Street Night Market. “Now, a lot of foreigners walk past, see my sign, and laugh. People just love kicking someone when they’re down.”
paras.zh: “他又不是杀了人，也不是放了火。为什么要小题大做？” 周一晚上，涂站在林江街夜市摊位的黄色灯光下说道。“现在，很多外国人走过，看到我的招牌，就笑。人们就喜欢落井下石。”

paras.en: At the entrance of his shop, Tu continues to proudly display a photo of Huang posing with him and his wife. “I think he’s such a warm and approachable person,” Tu added. “Why are people treating him this way?”
paras.zh: 在店门口，涂师傅仍旧自豪地展示着一张黄渤与他和妻子合影的照片。“我觉得他是一个非常热情、平易近人的人，”涂先生补充道。“为什么人们要这样对待他？”

paras.en: Tu says that Huang has visited his shop three times since 2023, and he always orders the same thing: mango shaved ice with tangyuan (sticky rice balls). The dessert, a blend of tropical fruit and condensed milk, is popular in Taipei’s bustling night markets, especially among first-time visitors to the island.
“When he came in for shaved ice, he would spend half an hour eating a single bowl,” recalled Tu. “Whenever someone came up to take a photo with him, he got right up. He’s not pretentious.”

At a tofu pudding shop near Ningxia Night Market in western Taipei, photos of Huang remain on display alongside those of other prominent technology figures who have visited, including Morris Chang, the founder of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). The store manager, Hsieh, defended the shop’s decision to keep them up.
“I don’t think this changes the fact that he’s a very successful businessman,” Hsieh said of Huang’s affairs with Alice Huang and other women. “Having an affair is a private matter.”

Hsieh, who agreed to be identified only by his surname for privacy reasons, said that Huang had visited the shop four times over the past few years, and on each occasion he seemed friendly and down-to-earth.

In Taiwan, Huang’s culinary indulgences extended well beyond street food. He frequented some of Taipei’s most exclusive restaurants, where he hosted technology executives for what became known in the local press as “Trillion-Dollar Banquets,” a reference to the attendees’ combined net worth of more than 1 trillion New Taiwan dollars.

The dinners often drew crowds of journalists and photographers hoping to catch a glimpse of Huang and his guests. The intense media attention helps explain why so many photographs and videos of Huang with Alice Huang were captured in Taiwan. Restaurant owners, meanwhile, welcomed the publicity, often proudly displaying photographs of themselves with Huang inside their establishments.

The Taiwanese tea chain 19 Tea House launched a new drink this week, giving it a name that pokes fun at Huang’s alleged “womanizing” ways. According to the chain, the drink combines osmanthus-infused honey with fresh lemon, offering a blend of fragrant floral notes and sweet-and-tangy citrus flavors.

Support for Huang in Taiwan has also extended far beyond the restaurants he frequented. On Monday evening, Taipei 101, the island’s iconic skyscraper just blocks from one of Huang’s favorite night markets, lit up with messages of support for the former Nvidia CEO, including “Taiwan ♡ Jensen,” “Family ♡ Friendship,” “Thrive Together,” and “Taiwan AI Build Future Together.”

Tech industry figures who supported the initiative told Taiwan’s state-run Central News Agency that the illumination campaign was intended to “help restore Jensen Huang’s reputation,” urging the public not to “kick him when he's down, but instead offer warmth and support during the autumn and winter.”

articles.title: The Best Hatch Black Friday Deals (2026)
articles.author: Boutayna Chokrane

paras.en: If you’re still using your iPhone’s “Radar” sound as an alarm, it might be time for an upgrade. The latest Hatch Sleep Clock is designed to make both falling asleep and waking up a little more pleasant. It combines a sunrise alarm clock, dimmable bedside light, sound machine, and contactless sleep tracking into one bedside gadget. And for the first time, it’s going on sale (early) as a Black Friday deal.
paras.zh: 如果您还在使用iPhone的“雷达”声音作为闹钟，也许是时候升级一下了。最新款Hatch睡眠闹钟旨在让入睡和醒来都变得更加惬意。它将日出闹钟、可调光床头灯、声音机和非接触式睡眠跟踪功能集成到一个床头小工具中。而且，它将首次（提前）作为黑色星期五特惠产品发售。

paras.en: From November 19 through November 20, the Sleep Clock is 25 percent off at Hatch and Amazon. Normally $250, it’s down to $188, which is just $18 more than the Hatch Restore 3’s $170 retail price. And unlike its predecessor, the newer Hatch adds passive sleep monitoring, which is pretty compelling for anyone who hates wearing wearables to bed. Or maybe you’re like me and occasionally forget to wear your Oura Ring to bed, in which case, you wouldn’t have to worry because the Hatch is already quietly tracking your sleep in the background.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: I’ve been testing the Hatch Sleep Clock for over two months, and it’s earned a permanent spot on my nightstand. As someone who already wears a smart ring and smartwatch to bed, I’m not exactly short on sleep-tracking data. But I’ve never owned a sunrise alarm clock, and I instantly became a convert. Unlike my iPhone or Amazon Echo Dot, it doesn’t wake me up by blaring an obnoxious alarm in my pitch-black bedroom. Instead, it gradually illuminates the room within my scheduled wake-up time. You can customize the sunrise's duration and brightness, and pair it with a soundscape of your choosing. It truly makes getting out of bed feel less jarring, especially as the mornings get darker.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Most notably, the Sleep Clock also doubles as a contactless sleep tracker, using a built-in motion sensor to detect your movements and breathing throughout the night. I compared its readings against my Oura Ring 5 and Apple Watch Series 12, and while sleep duration estimates were generally aligned, the sleep-stage readings were less consistent. The device doesn’t measure physiological metrics like heart rate, and it can’t detect snoring or other audio-based sleep disruptions. I also found that placement significantly matters. My nightstand tends to collect clutter, so I had to rearrange my trinkets to make room for the clock.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Each morning, the Hatch app gives you a breakdown of when you went to bed, when you fell asleep, when you woke up, and how much time you spent in different sleep stages. The color-coded reports are easy to understand without burying me in random metrics. Plus, unlike most sleep trackers, Hatch doesn't require a subscription to access your sleep data. (You will need that Hatch+ membership ($6 per month) if you want to access the full audio library, however.)
paras.zh: 每天早上，Hatch应用程序都会向您提供详细的睡眠数据，包括您何时上床睡觉、何时入睡、何时醒来以及您在不同睡眠阶段所花费的时间。采用颜色编码的报告易于理解，不会让我淹没在杂乱无章的指标中。此外，与大多数睡眠跟踪器不同，Hatch无需订阅即可访问您的睡眠数据。（不过，如果您想访问完整的音频库，则需要Hatch+会员资格（每月6美元）。）

paras.en: Overall, the Hatch Sleep Clock is the best all-in-one bedside device. I wouldn’t recommend replacing your dedicated wearable with it if detailed health tracking is your priority. But if you’ve been wanting a sunrise alarm clock that can also offer a little insight into your sleep, do not sleep on this Black Friday deal.
paras.zh: 总体而言，Hatch睡眠闹钟是最佳的一体化床头设备。如果您优先考虑详细的健康跟踪，我不建议您用它来替代您的专用可穿戴设备。但如果您一直想要一款既能提供日出闹钟功能，又能对您的睡眠情况提供一些洞察的设备，千万不要错过这次黑色星期五的优惠。

paras.en: If you don’t care for sleep tracking, Hatch is also offering discounts on several other products across its lineup.
paras.zh: 如果您对睡眠监测不感兴趣，Hatch 旗下系列的其他几款产品也有折扣。

articles.title: Here’s the Date the 2026 Kennedy Center Honors Will Air on CBS
articles.author: Paul Grein

paras.en: The Kennedy Center Honors will air on Sunday, Dec. 27 (8:30-10:30 p.m. ET/8:00-10:00 p.m. PT) on CBS. The show will also stream live on Paramount+ (Premium) and will be available on demand. CBS has been the broadcast home of the Kennedy Center Honors since the first ceremony in 1978, but the delay in announcing that CBS would carry the show again this year raised a question about the current status of the relationship.
paras.zh: 肯尼迪中心荣誉奖颁奖典礼将于12月27日星期日（美国东部时间晚上8:30-10:30/美国太平洋时间晚上8:00-10:00）在CBS播出。该颁奖典礼还将在Paramount+（高级版）上直播，并提供点播服务。自1978年首届颁奖典礼以来，CBS一直是肯尼迪中心荣誉奖的播出平台，但今年CBS延迟宣布将再次播出该节目，这引发了人们对双方当前关系状况的疑问。

paras.en: No host has been named, which is also unusual less than three weeks before the event. President Trump hosted last year’s show, marking the first time a sitting president has hosted the show. The show will be held on Monday, Dec. 7, at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C. This will mark the first time the Honors haven’t been presented at the Kennedy Center, which is shut down for repairs.
paras.zh: 距离活动不到三周，但尚未宣布主持人人选，这也显得有些不寻常。特朗普总统主持了去年的颁奖典礼，这是在任总统首次主持该颁奖典礼。颁奖典礼将于12月7日（星期一）在华盛顿特区的凯匹德一号体育馆（Capital One Arena）举行。这将是肯尼迪中心首次不举办该颁奖典礼，因为该中心正在关闭维修。

paras.en: Three of this year’s recipients are best known for music – Country Music Hall of Fame member Barbara Mandrell, Songwriters Hall of Fame member Paul Anka and 16-time Grammy-winning producer and composer David Foster. A fourth honoree, Andy Garcia, is best known for acting, but is also a Grammy-winning music producer. The fifth honoree is Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright David Mamet.
paras.zh: 今年的三位获奖者以音乐闻名——乡村音乐名人堂成员芭芭拉·曼德瑞尔（Barbara Mandrell）、歌曲作者名人堂成员保罗·安卡（Paul Anka）以及16次格莱美奖获奖制作人兼作曲家大卫·福斯特（David Foster）。第四位获奖者安迪·加西亚（Andy Garcia）以演技闻名，但也是一位格莱美获奖音乐制作人。第五位获奖者是普利策奖获奖剧作家大卫·马梅特。

paras.en: The telecast will be produced by Den of Thieves, with Jesse Ignjatovic and Evan Prager as executive producers, and Barb Bialkowski as executive producer and showrunner. Micah Bickham will serve as director.
paras.zh: 该电视节目将由Den of Thieves制作，Jesse Ignjatovic和Evan Prager担任执行制片人，Barb Bialkowski担任执行制片人和节目总监。Micah Bickham将担任导演。

paras.en: Cheche Alara, Grammy and Latin Grammy-winning composer and producer, will serve as music producer and music director.
paras.zh: 格莱美奖和拉丁格莱美奖获奖作曲家兼制作人Cheche Alara将担任音乐制作人和音乐总监。

paras.en: CBS is the exclusive sponsor of the Kennedy Center Honors. Boeing is the exclusive underwriter of the Kennedy Center Honors Gala.
paras.zh: 哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）是肯尼迪中心荣誉奖的独家赞助商。波音公司是肯尼迪中心荣誉晚宴的独家承销商。

paras.en: A limited number of tickets to the 49th Kennedy Center Honors, a black-tie gala, will be available to the general public on Monday, November 23, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. ET through the Kennedy Center’s website.
paras.zh: 第49届肯尼迪中心荣誉奖是一场盛装晚宴，面向公众的少量门票将于美国东部时间2026年11月23日（星期一）上午10:00通过肯尼迪中心的网站发售。

articles.title: 2026 CMA Awards: 6 Things You Didn’t See on TV
articles.author: Anna Chan

paras.en: Typically, when someone wins multiple trophies during the CMA Awards, they end up holding all of the crystal hardware in their arms in the press room backstage, providing a visual image of their bounty for photographers covering the event.
paras.zh: 通常，当有人在CMA颁奖典礼上赢得多个奖杯时，他们最终会在后台的媒体室里抱着所有水晶奖杯，为报道该活动的摄影师提供他们收获的视觉形象。

paras.en: When Ella Langley stepped onto the press room stage after winning a record-setting six honors during the CMA’s 60th annual ceremony held at Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena on Wednesday (Nov. 18), she didn’t even attempt that pose — presumably, the risk of dropping that many was too great to try it. Instead, they lined up the pointy pieces along the front of the stage, almost as if they were footlights.
paras.zh: 周三（11月18日），在纳什维尔的普利司通体育馆举行的CMA第60届年度颁奖典礼上，埃拉·兰利（Ella Langley）创纪录地斩获六项大奖，随后登上新闻发布会舞台时，她甚至没有尝试摆出那个姿势——大概是因为奖杯太多，掉落的风险太大，所以不敢尝试。相反，她将这些尖尖的奖杯排成一排放在舞台前方，看起来几乎就像脚灯一样。

paras.en: Langley, of course, was omnipresent during the evening, delivering so many acceptance speeches that when she collected entertainer of the year at the end of the night, she confessed, “At this point, I’m sick of me.”
paras.zh: 当然，Langley当晚无处不在，发表了如此多的获奖感言，以至于当她在晚会结束时领取年度艺人奖时，她坦言：“此时此刻，我已经厌倦了自己。”

paras.en: Her six wins included three that specifically recognized “Choosin’ Texas” — single, song and music video of the year — and they came in a week where that tune is dominating. It led her to seven Grammy nominations on Nov. 16; spurred BMI to initiate an Impact Award, presented to Langley and cowriters Miranda Lambert, Joybeth Taylor and Luke Dick during the performing rights organization’s country awards on Nov. 17; and is likely to tie the all-time record for most weeks at No. 1 on Billboard’s Hot Country Songs when chart numbers are announced Thanksgiving week, based on this week’s data.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: It was one of numerous topics addressed off-camera before — and during — the ABC telecast. Here are six things you didn’t see on TV.
paras.zh: 这是在ABC电视台直播之前和直播期间在镜头外讨论的众多话题之一。以下是您在电视上没有看到的六件事。

paras.en: - Ella Langley Discusses the Success of “Choosin’ Texas” “Choosin’ Texas” is enjoying a historic run, thanks to an ingratiating melody and a storyline that puts the resignation of a broken heart in a subtly unique perspective. But what’s the secret sauce that led to its success? Its four writers are either playing their cards close to the vest or — much more likely — are as perplexed as everyone else. “I don’t know exactly what it is,” Langley told reporters in the press room. “I really don’t. I just make music that I love. I make music, when I’m in the room writing it, that makes me and my cowriters smile or cry or feel like we’re getting through something we need to, and that’s really all we do.” Surely, when isolated on the red carpet, Luke Dick could give a little extra insight. But he couldn’t nail it down either. “If you could codify the magic, people would bottle it and sell it in every country,” Dick told Billboard. “It’s just place and time and magic, and then it comes out, and everybody says, ‘We knew it all along’ after the fact. But the truth is, we were just four people having fun, writing songs that felt good to us at the time, not chasing anything and just being ourselves.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - Miranda Lambert Offers Advice on How to Use Heartache That whole idea that a creator has to suffer for their art has been debated for eons. Suffering, of course, has been central to the country genre since its inception — “Will the Circle Be Unbroken,” which finds gospel positivity amidst a funeral and burial, is one of its bedrock theme songs. Miranda Lambert, who won trophies as a cowriter and coproducer of “Choosin’ Texas,” acknowledged the commercial value of misery, but doesn’t exactly advocate for artistic martyrdom. “We got to use heartache as a muse,” she told reporters. “You know, we got to feel it, wallow in it a little bit — ‘waller’ in it, as we say in Texas — and then move the hell on.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - Devin Dawson Gets Out of His Comfort Zone Devin Dawson won his first CMA trophy after coproducing one track, “Loving Life Again,” on Langley’s album of the year, Dandelion, but his awards night wasn’t all glitter. One of the screw-on caps on a shiny, silver collar bar he was wearing fell off before the show, and when he discovered the mishap, five or six handlers joined him in scouring the crowded carpet for that one small nodule. Happily, they did find it. Dawson meanwhile is getting closer to finding his voice. He earned his first hit in 2017 with “All On Me,” and got a No. 1 in 2020 by teaming with HARDY and Lauren Alaina on “One Beer.” He’s been sidelined, though, for several years with vocal issues. He may soon be back. “Singing isn’t as free as I wish it was,” he told Billboard on the carpet. “I don’t have as much control as I wish I did, but I’m working on it and I’m getting myself out of the comfort zone. I’m producing a song right now that Mitchell Tenpenny, ERNEST and myself wrote, and we’re all going to feature on it together — I think, probably, for Mitchell’s album. If it comes out, it’ll be the first thing I put out in a while.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - HARDY Reveals How He Stays Inspired Historically, kids in households across America have watched awards shows with a dream that maybe they could end up winning a trophy. That’s true for pretty much every artist at the CMAs. Vince Gill, 69, noted backstage that he may have seen, or participated in, each of the organization’s ceremonies. But it’s lonely at the top, as the saying goes, and HARDY is one of the artists who’s worked to keep his feet on the ground by spending time back in Philadelphia, Miss., where he grew up. HARDY’s “McArthur” — a collaboration with Eric Church, Morgan Wallen and Tim McGraw — won musical event of the year behind a plot about a family handing down its land across generations. Thus, it’s in character that he has a place in his soul for a more ordinary life, which in turn fuels his music. “I keep up with my buddies back home and what they’re doing,” he said in the press room. “I kind of live vicariously through them sometimes. Their lives are very different than mine, but I always feel like a lot of the songs that I write are through my friends back home and the lives that they’re living because I don’t really get to do that anymore. That’s OK, but keeping track of my hometown … is a big way to keep me inspired.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - Charlie Worsham Celebrates Scott Colom’s Election Victory Charlie Worsham, due to join the Grand Ole Opry on Dec. 1, won his second musician of the year award in the last three years. The victory was sandwiched around steel guitarist Paul Franklin’s win last year, after 32 previous nominations. Worsham advocated more than once during the evening for Franklin to earn a spot in the Country Music Hall of Fame. But Worsham is also celebrating his home state. He went to school in Grenada, Miss., where his parents had seen the violence and tension that accompanied desegregation during the Civil Rights Era. With that heritage, Worsham is still buzzing over Scott Colom’s election as a state senator earlier in November. “I am beside myself,” he told Billboard on the red carpet. “It is the first Black representative of our state in the Senate since the 1880s. Scott Colom just seems to have the charisma and the heart. He seems to be in it for the right reasons. And regardless of party, this is something we should all be celebrating … There has always been a Mississippi that we could become, and now, I’m really believing that we just might do it.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - Stephen Wilson Jr. Explains “God the Source” Several artists thanked Jesus Christ during their CMA acceptance speeches — not an unusual occurrence during the awards — but Stephen Wilson Jr., as he walked off with new artist of the year, reframed that thought, acknowledging “God the Source” from the podium. A self-described “recovering microbiologist,” Wilson Jr. explained the comment in the press room. God, not surprisingly, is every bit as elusive as the key to the success of “Choosin’ Texas.” “The Source is undefinable,” he philosophized. “To me, art and the Source are the same thing. Like, art without the Source is not art at all. The songs that I write come from somewhere else that I don’t pretend to understand — that’s the alchemy that attracted me to music in the first place. I went and studied organic chemistry and physics, and tried to understand everything at a molecular level … But there’s something very, very special about the alchemy of music that is really beyond comprehension. Scientists try to comprehend everything, [but] science is holding on, and music is letting go. I have chosen to let go, and it has led me here.”

paras.en: Since 2013, fans have been eagerly waiting for the follow-up to GTA 5. And 13 years later, Rockstar Games finally delivered with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI for Sony PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

articles.title: CBS Inks New Deal to Air Kennedy Center Honors
articles.author: Etan Vlessing

paras.en: The Kennedy Center Honors will air on CBS once again this year, despite the longtime network home’s pact to air the awards ceremony expiring after last year’s broadcast aired.
paras.zh: 尽管该电视台与肯尼迪中心荣誉奖的长期合作协议在去年颁奖典礼播出后已到期，但今年的颁奖典礼仍将在CBS播出。

paras.en: CBS has inked a new deal to televise the event, which will also stream live on Paramount+ (Premium), on Dec. 27 after the awards themselves take place on Dec. 7.
paras.zh: CBS已签署一项新协议，将于12月27日对该颁奖典礼进行电视转播，该典礼还将于12月7日当天在Paramount+（高级版）上进行直播。

paras.en: The 2026 Kennedy Center Honors will take place at Capital One Arena in Washington D.C., not the Kennedy Center itself. The new digs for the Kennedy Center Honors follows a shut down of the Kennedy Center and efforts by President Donald Trump to rename the arts institution.
paras.zh: 2026年肯尼迪中心荣誉奖颁奖典礼将在华盛顿特区的凯匹勒中心体育馆举行，而不是在肯尼迪中心。肯尼迪中心荣誉奖的新场地选定是在肯尼迪中心关闭以及唐纳德·特朗普总统试图为该艺术机构更名之后。

paras.en: There’s no word on whether Trump will again host the 2026 Kennedy Center Honors event.
paras.zh: 目前尚不清楚特朗普是否会再次主持2026年肯尼迪中心荣誉奖颁奖典礼。

paras.en: Previously announced honorees include Paul Anka, David Foster, Andy Garcia, David Mamet and Barbara Mandrell. CBS taking on broadcast duties for the 2026 Kennedy Center Honors follows last year’s event, hosted by Trump, being the lowest-rated Kennedy Center Honors telecast. Still, the Kennedy Center defended the show’s popularity, noting that it aired two days before Christmas and didn’t have the Sunday spot, with an NFL lead-in, that the 2024 broadcast had enjoyed.
paras.zh: 此前已宣布的获奖者包括保罗·安卡、大卫·福斯特、安迪·加西亚、大卫·马梅特和芭芭拉·曼德雷尔。CBS将负责2026年肯尼迪中心荣誉奖的转播工作，此前由特朗普主持的去年颁奖典礼是肯尼迪中心荣誉奖收视率最低的一次转播。尽管如此，肯尼迪中心仍为该节目的受欢迎程度辩护，指出该节目在圣诞节前两天播出，没有像2024年那样在周日播出，且没有NFL的预热节目。

paras.en: CBS has televised every Kennedy Center Honors since 1978, but the last deal ended with the 2026 broadcast. And CBS’ exclusive negotiating window lapsed in 2025, opening up the potential pool of bidders.
paras.zh: 自1978年以来，CBS一直负责肯尼迪中心荣誉奖的电视转播，但上一份合同已于2026年转播结束后到期。CBS 的独家谈判窗口将于 2025 年到期，这将为潜在竞标者敞开大门。

paras.en: The low ratings, however, wasn’t initially hurting interest in TV or streaming rights for the ceremony, The Hollywood Reporter revealed in January.
paras.zh: 然而，《好莱坞报道》在1月份透露，低收视率最初并未影响人们对颁奖典礼的电视或流媒体播放权的兴趣。

paras.en: “Several outlets want to get the next contract — and CBS says they won’t lose it,” a source told THR at the time.
paras.zh: “多家媒体都想拿下下一份合同，而CBS表示他们不会失去这份合同。”一位消息人士当时对《好莱坞报道者》表示。

paras.en: The Kennedy Center itself has been at the center of a legal battle as Trump slammed a court decision to block his name, twice, from being added to the building’s exterior. The board at the arts institution also chose to shut down the Kennedy Center, with Trump in social media posts suggesting the closure would allow future renovations.
paras.zh: 肯尼迪中心本身也陷入了一场法律纠纷的漩涡，因为特朗普曾两次抨击法院的裁决，该裁决禁止将他的名字添加到该建筑的外墙上。该艺术机构的董事会也决定关闭肯尼迪中心，而特朗普在社交媒体帖子中表示，关闭该中心将为今后的翻修铺平道路。

paras.en: Trump’s close interest in and involvement with Kennedy Center events, since he first added his name to the exterior of the building in a controversial move at the end of 2025, was a wild card in dealmaking.
paras.zh: 自2005年底以一种有争议的方式将自己的名字加到该建筑的外墙上以来，特朗普对肯尼迪中心的活动一直表现出浓厚的兴趣并积极参与其中，这在交易中起到了出人意料的作用。

paras.en: The 49th Kennedy Center Honors will be produced by Den of Thieves, with Jesse Ignjatovic and Evan Prager as executive producers, and Barb Bialkowski as executive producer and showrunner.
paras.zh: 第49届肯尼迪中心荣誉颁奖礼将由Den of Thieves制作，Jesse Ignjatovic和Evan Prager担任执行制片人，Barb Bialkowski担任执行制片人和节目总监。

paras.en: Directing the special will be Micah Bickham, while Cheche Alara will serve as music producer and music director.
paras.zh: Micah Bickham将担任特别节目的导演，而Cheche Alara将担任音乐制作人和音乐总监。

articles.title: ‘GTA 6’ Sales Have Already Surpassed Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’
articles.author: James Hibberd

paras.en: For those wondering why Rockstar Games hasn’t licensed Grand Theft Auto for a movie or TV show, this is probably why.
paras.zh: 对于那些想知道为什么Rockstar Games没有将《侠盗猎车手》授权给电影或电视剧的人来说，这可能是原因所在。

paras.en: Grand Theft Auto VI has already generated an incredible $1.84 billion in sales, according to market intelligence firm Sensor Tower.
paras.zh: 据市场情报公司Sensor Tower的数据，侠盗猎车手6（Grand Theft Auto VI）的销售额已达到惊人的18.4亿美元。

paras.en: That’s more than Christopher Nolan‘s blockbuster The Odyssey made during its entire global run ($1.80 billion).
paras.zh: 这比克里斯托弗·诺兰（Christopher Nolan）的票房大片《奥德赛》（The Odyssey）在全球上映期间的总票房（18亿美元）还要高。

paras.en: What’s more amazing, is GTA 6‘s eye-popping sales figure may already be outdated. While Sensor Tower updated its tracker Thursday, the underlying charts appear to only show pre-sales through Tuesday — meaning that $1.84 billion estimate doesn’t yet account for yesterday (when all those glowing reviews were published) or today (when the game was actually released).
paras.zh: 更令人惊叹的是，《GTA 6》令人瞠目结舌的销售额可能已经过时了。虽然Sensor Tower于周四更新了其跟踪器，但底层的图表似乎只显示了截至周二的预售情况——这意味着18.4亿美元的估算尚未计入昨天（所有那些好评如潮的评价发布之时）或今天（游戏正式发布之时）的数据。

paras.en: Therefore, current GTA 6 sales is very likely over $2 billion (in case you’re curious, the revenue split is 75 percent from PS5 sales and 25 percent for Xbox).
paras.zh: 因此，目前的 GTA 6 销售额很可能超过 20 亿美元（如果你好奇的话，收入分成是 PS5 销售额的 75% 和 Xbox 的 25%）。

paras.en: And GTA games tend to have very, very long tails. GTA 5 was released 13 years ago and has generated an estimated $5.4 billion in lifetime revenue (plus an additional $5.4 billion in revenue during that period from GTA Online), according to The Wall Street Journal. Even over the last four years, GTA 5 has averaged $400 million in sales … for, again, a game released in 2013. The top-grossing movie in 2013 was Disney’s Frozen, which made $1.28 billion … now imagine if last year Frozen was still averaging $400 million a year in ticket sales.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: So needless to say, GTA 6 is just getting started.
paras.zh: 不用说，GTA 6 才刚刚开始。

paras.en: Going back to that question up top, Rockstar Games is likely disinclined to risk its brand value or reputation through a movie or TV project given the revenue for the company would probably end up being a pretty small fraction of what they already make from the game itself.
paras.zh: 回到前面的问题，考虑到公司从电影或电视剧项目中获得的收入可能最终只占游戏本身收入的一小部分，Rockstar Games很可能不愿意通过电影或电视剧项目来冒险损害其品牌价值或声誉。

paras.en: As Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Rockstar’s parent company Take-Two Interactive, told The David Rubenstein Show earlier this month: “We’re very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth, entertainment we’re always proud of. We would make a movie or television show based on our intellectual property if our creative teams were passionate about it, if they thought they would somehow engage and delight our consumers. It’s a high bar to do that. And of course, there’s always a risk of failure. So we don’t rule it out, but we’re very, very selective.”

articles.title: Amazon app warns New York of higher costs if Mamdani delivery law passes

paras.en: Amazon is taking its fight against a New York City delivery bill, which has been backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, to its shopping website and app.
paras.zh: 亚马逊正在其购物网站和应用程序上发起对纽约市一项派送法案的抗争，该法案得到了市议员佐兰·马姆达尼的支持。

paras.en: Some users who open the company's shopping app or website report being served with pop-ups and banners warning that the New York City Council "could add up to $5 per order" if it passes Intro 518, or the Delivery Protection Act.
paras.zh: 一些打开该公司购物应用程序或网站的用户报告称，他们收到了弹出窗口和横幅，警告称，如果纽约市议会通过了 Intro 518 或《送货保护法案》，“每个订单可能会增加最多 5 美元”。

paras.en: The bill would require Amazon to employ its army of third-party delivery companies directly, disrupting the contractor model it has relied on since 2018. Amazon uses a network of thousands of small companies, which often work solely for Amazon, to handle the last-mile portion of shipments, in an effort to speed up deliveries and control more of its logistics operations.
paras.zh: 该法案将要求亚马逊直接雇用其第三方送货公司，这将颠覆其自 2018 年以来一直依赖的承包商模式。亚马逊利用由数千家小公司组成的网络（这些公司通常只为亚马逊服务）来处理最后一英里的货运部分，以加快送货速度并控制更多的物流业务。

paras.en: "If this legislation passes, we'd no longer be able to work with them, and we'd be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city," Amazon's in-app message states. "That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees."
paras.zh: 亚马逊在应用程序内的消息称：“如果这项立法通过，我们将无法再与他们合作，我们将被迫考虑将我们的业务转移到城外。” “这可能意味着纽约市数百万客户的送货速度会更慢、成本更高，同时也会威胁到小企业及其数千名员工。”

paras.en: The proposed legislation was introduced in February and is awaiting review by City Council Speaker Julie Menin.
paras.zh: 拟议的立法于二月提出，正在等待市议会议长朱莉·梅宁的审查。

paras.en: Amazon also posted a statement on its company website where it often publishes its policy positions. But rarely has the company used its valuable e-commerce site and app real estate to push its perspectives. Other tech companies including Uber and Lyft have similarly used their apps to advocate for or against legislation in the past.
paras.zh: 亚马逊还在其公司网站上发布了一份声明，该公司经常在该网站上发布其政策立场。但该公司很少利用其宝贵的电子商务网站和应用程序资产来推动其观点。包括 Uber 和 Lyft 在内的其他科技公司过去也曾类似地使用他们的应用程序来支持或反对立法。

paras.en: Amazon's pop-up notices and a stationary banner on its store homepage direct users to a form where they can "contact your council member to oppose Intro 518."
paras.zh: 亚马逊的弹出式通知和商店主页上的固定横幅将用户引导至一个表格，他们可以在其中“联系您的理事会成员反对 Intro 518”。

paras.en: According to Amazon, 20,000 customers sent emails to city council members in the first six hours that the pop-up appeared.
paras.zh: 据亚马逊称，在弹出窗口出现后的前六个小时内，有2万名顾客向市议会成员发送了电子邮件。

paras.en: Menin told CNBC in a statement that Amazon's claim it will need to raise prices due to the proposed legislation "defies logic."
paras.zh: 梅宁在一份声明中告诉 CNBC，亚马逊声称由于拟议的立法而需要提高价格“不符合逻辑”。

paras.en: "We are crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs," Menin said. "If Amazon thinks this deceptive campaign will effectively threaten New Yorkers and intimidate this City Council, they are dead wrong."
paras.zh: “我们正在制定立法来监管亚马逊并保护工人，而不影响价格或就业，”梅宁说。 “如果亚马逊认为这种欺骗性活动将有效地威胁纽约人并恐吓市议会，那么他们就大错特错了。”

paras.en: Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel said in a statement that the company put up the notices to be "transparent with our customers" about what the bill "would cause them if it passes as written."
paras.zh: 亚马逊发言人Kelly Nantel在一份声明中表示，公司发布这些通知是为了“向顾客坦诚告知”该法案“如果按原样通过，将对他们造成怎样的影响”。

paras.en: "If customers are concerned, one of the most impactful things they can do is contact their City Council member and ask them to oppose this bill," Nantel said.
paras.zh: 南特尔说：“如果顾客担心，他们能做的最有影响力的事情之一就是联系市议会成员并要求他们反对这项法案。”

paras.en: The Delivery Protection Act has received a swell of support from labor groups, including the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, which has sought to unionize Amazon delivery and warehouse workers.
paras.zh: 《派送保障法案》得到了包括国际卡车司机兄弟会（International Brotherhood of Teamsters）在内的多个劳工团体的鼎力支持，该组织一直致力于为亚马逊的派送和仓库工人组建工会。

paras.en: Mamdani endorsed the bill in August, saying Amazon's subcontractor model "leaves workers vulnerable and corporations free to avoid accountability for reckless conditions on city streets." He's argued the bill would lead to safer working conditions for drivers, and allow the city to "regulate last-mile operations."
paras.zh: Mamdani 于 8 月表示支持该法案，称亚马逊的分包商模式“使工人处于弱势地位，而公司则可以随意逃避对城市街道上不负责任的状况承担责任”。他认为，该法案将为司机带来更安全的工作条件，并使市政府能够“监管最后一公里的运营”。

paras.en: Amazon disputed Mamdani's claims, saying the bill would put Delivery Service Partner jobs "at risk without improving safety." It also argued that other businesses and governments use contractors in their operations, and said the DSP model has allowed it to meet growing customer demand.
paras.zh: 亚马逊对Mamdani的说法提出异议，称该法案将使派送服务合作伙伴的职位“面临风险，而不会改善安全性”。亚马逊还指出，其他企业和政府在运营中也使用承包商，并表示DSP模式使其能够满足不断增长的客户需求。

paras.en: "It works because local entrepreneurs — people rooted in their communities — deliver a better experience," Amazon said. "They invest in their teams, their routes, and their neighborhoods. That's not a liability play."
paras.zh: 亚马逊表示：“它之所以有效，是因为当地企业家——植根于社区的人们——提供了更好的体验。” “他们投资于他们的团队、他们的路线和他们的社区。这不是一种责任游戏。”

paras.en: Amazon has lobbied heavily against the bill, while logistics and business groups have launched local advertising campaigns, and warned they may sue the city if the bill passes.
paras.zh: 亚马逊大力游说反对该法案，而物流和商业团体则发起了当地广告活动，并警告说，如果该法案通过，他们可能会起诉该市。

articles.title: Anthropic IPO live updates: AI lab tops $2 trillion market cap after record offering

paras.en: Anthropic's stock rose 17% in the artificial intelligence lab's Nasdaq debut on Thursday after the company completed the biggest initial public offering on record.
paras.zh: 周四，人工智能实验室 Anthropic 在纳斯达克上市，该公司完成了有记录以来最大的首次公开募股，其股价上涨了 17%。

paras.en: The stock is trading under ticker symbol "ANT" after the company raised $81.3 billion in the IPO. The Claude creator sold 980 million shares at $83 a piece on Wednesday, lifting the size and price of its offering. The shares opened at $111.50 before selling off during the day.
paras.zh: 该公司在 IPO 中筹集了 813 亿美元资金，股票代码为“ANT”。周三，克劳德创始人以每股 83 美元的价格出售了 9.8 亿股股票，提高了发行规模和发行价格。该股开盘价为 111.50 美元，随后全天遭到抛售。

paras.en: The 5-year-old company captivated the corporate world with its Claude AI models and products, which have fueled its meteoric rise this year. Anthropic said in its prospectus that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up a staggering 1,200% from the same period last year.
paras.zh: 这家成立5年的公司凭借其Claude AI模型和产品吸引了企业界，并助推了其今年的迅速崛起。 Anthropic 在招股说明书中表示，截至 9 月 30 日的 9 个月内，其收入为 332.4 亿美元，比去年同期增长了 1,200%，令人震惊。

paras.en: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI, now its chief rival. Anthropic has faced sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, including by President Donald Trump and other senior government officials.
paras.zh: Anthropic首席执行官Dario Amodei在2021年与一小群研究人员从OpenAI（现为其主要竞争对手）跳槽后共同创立了这家公司。Anthropic在其安全、监管和国家安全方面的立场上受到了尖锐的批评，包括来自唐纳德·特朗普总统和其他高级政府官员的批评。

paras.en: - Ashton Kutcher congratulates the AI lab
paras.zh: - Ashton Kutcher 祝贺人工智能实验室

paras.en: - Market cap tops $2 trillion in debut, putting it among the tech titans
paras.zh: - 首次上市市值突破 2 万亿美元，跻身科技巨头之列

paras.en: - Daniela Amodei gives a shoutout to mom
paras.zh: - 丹妮拉·阿莫代 (Daniela Amodei) 向妈妈大声喊叫

paras.en: - Dario Amodei addresses debt and landing an investment-grade credit rating
paras.zh: - 达里奥·阿莫代 (Dario Amodei) 解决债务问题并获得投资级信用评级

paras.en: - Spotted: Executives sporting "Clawd" pins at Nasdaq
paras.zh: - 被发现：纳斯达克高管佩戴“Clawd”徽章

paras.en: - Dario Amodei renews pledge to pace frontier AI development
paras.zh: - Dario Amodei 重申加快前沿人工智能发展的承诺

paras.en: - Retail demand for ANT was the largest in history
paras.zh: - ANT 的零售需求创历史新高

paras.en: CNBC's reporters are covering Anthropic's IPO live on air and online from our bureaus in San Francisco and Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, and from the Nasdaq in New York City.
paras.zh: CNBC的记者正在从我们位于旧金山和新泽西州恩格尔伍德克利夫的办事处以及纽约市的纳斯达克现场和在线报道Anthropic的IPO。

articles.title: Palo Alto stock jumps on earnings beat and company's big bet on securing open-weight models

paras.en: Palo Alto Networks shares rose 6% on Thursday as businesses boosted spending on cybersecurity products and investors cheered the company's acquisition of a startup that pushes it into securing open-weight artificial intelligence models.
paras.zh: Palo Alto Networks 股价周四上涨 6%，原因是企业增加了网络安全产品的支出，并且投资者对该公司收购一家初创公司表示欢迎，该公司推动其确保开放权重人工智能模型的安全。

paras.en: The company beat Wall Street's estimates for the fiscal first quarter. Revenue jumped 39% from a year ago and Palo Alto lifted its guidance for the year.
paras.zh: 该公司第一财季的表现超出了华尔街的预期。收入较去年同期增长 39%，帕洛阿尔托上调了今年的指引。

paras.en: Recent outages at Microsoft, banks and the Federal Aviation Administration have left businesses reeling. While U.S. officials haven't detected any malicious activity, the disruptions raise concerns over aging equipment and infrastructure. Many businesses are scrambling to patch vulnerabilities at a faster clip than ever before to keep pace with the growing risks of AI-powered cyberattacks.
paras.zh: 微软、银行和联邦航空管理局最近出现的服务中断让企业陷入困境。尽管美国官员尚未发现任何恶意活动，但这些中断引发了人们对设备和基础设施老化的担忧。许多企业正以前所未有的速度争先恐后地修补漏洞，以应对人工智能驱动的网络攻击日益增长的风险。

paras.en: Those fears have led more businesses to consolidate platforms, which is fueling growth in areas like firewall and AI security, Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora told CNBC's "Mad Money" on Wednesday.
paras.zh: Palo Alto Networks 首席执行官 Nikesh Arora 周三在 CNBC 的“Mad Money”节目中表示，这些担忧导致更多企业整合平台，从而推动防火墙和人工智能安全等领域的增长。

paras.en: "They're going to have to make sure they get the best players in the market to come support them because this is no longer child's play," Arora said.
paras.zh: “他们必须确保获得市场上最好的球员来支持他们，因为这不再是儿戏，”阿罗拉说。

paras.en: Alongside earnings, Palo Alto announced a $4.5 billion deal to buy Applied Compute, a startup that helps train customized open-weight models. It's one of several recent deals in Arora's aggressive acquisition spree and marks a significant shift beyond cybersecurity.
paras.zh: 除了盈利之外，帕洛阿尔托还宣布斥资 45 亿美元收购 Applied Compute，这是一家帮助训练定制开放权重模型的初创公司。这是 Arora 最近大举收购的几笔交易之一，标志着网络安全领域的重大转变。

paras.en: "Rather than being one player out of 10 in the industry serving compute, we want to be the one player with Palo Alto that delivers secure compute and security capability," Arora told CNBC.
paras.zh: Arora 告诉 CNBC：“我们不想成为计算服务行业中十分之一的参与者，而是希望成为 Palo Alto 提供安全计算和安全功能的参与者之一。”

paras.en: Palo Alto expects the deal to add more than $1 billion in annual recurring revenue to its next-generation security business by the 2029 fiscal year.
paras.zh: Palo Alto 预计，到 2029 财年，该交易将为其下一代安全业务带来超过 10 亿美元的年度经常性收入。

paras.en: Analysts at Bank of America touted the deal as a "bold move" to expand beyond securing AI into training open-weight models, allowing Palo Alto to lead the next phase of the AI revolution.
paras.zh: 美国银行的分析师称赞这笔交易是“大胆的举动”，将人工智能扩展到训练开放权重模型，从而使帕洛阿尔托能够引领人工智能革命的下一阶段。

paras.en: This "appears consistent with PANW's 'long-game' - become indispensable beyond cyber into multidisciplinary IT domains across AI-value-chain," wrote analysts at Citigroup.
paras.zh: 花旗集团的分析师写道，这“似乎与 PANW 的‘长期目标’一致——超越网络领域，进入跨人工智能价值链的多学科 IT 领域。”

articles.title: ‘A watershed moment’: Researchers unveil first-of-its-kind blood test for CTE

paras.en: A first-of-its-kind blood test for chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) may be just around the corner. Scientists say the new method, if validated in large studies, could help doctors spot and treat the disease, which has long been notoriously difficult to study and has only ever been diagnosed after death.
paras.zh: 首次针对慢性创伤性脑病（CTE）的血液检测可能即将到来。科学家表示，这种新方法如果在大型研究中得到验证，可以帮助医生发现和治疗这种疾病，这种疾病长期以来一直难以研究，而且只有在死后才能被诊断出来。

paras.en: CTE is a devastating neurodegenerative disease linked to repeated head trauma—including collisions in sports such as American football—and can cause mood swings, behavior changes, memory issues, and more. One of the challenges with studying CTE, however, is that it currently can only be diagnosed by autopsy after a person dies. That makes it difficult to know who has CTE—never mind how to treat it.
paras.zh: CTE 是一种毁灭性的神经退行性疾病，与反复的头部创伤（包括美式橄榄球等运动中的碰撞）有关，可能导致情绪波动、行为改变、记忆问题等。然而，研究 CTE 的挑战之一是，目前只能在人死后通过尸检来诊断。这使得我们很难知道谁患有 CTE，更不用说如何治疗它了。

paras.en: That could soon change. In a new study published in the Journal of the American Medical Association on Thursday, researchers analyzed blood samples from 21 football players who donated their brains to science, 18 of whom were found to have varying stages of CTE after their deaths. The researchers determined that specific biomarkers found in their blood could identify the most severe CTE cases.
paras.zh: 这种情况可能很快就会改变。在周四发表在《美国医学会杂志》上的一项新研究中，研究人员分析了 21 名将大脑捐献给科学的足球运动员的血液样本，发现其中 18 名球员死后患有不同阶段的 CTE。研究人员确定，在他们的血液中发现的特定生物标志物可以识别最严重的 CTE 病例。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The test is not approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, cautions Michael Alosco, the study’s senior author and co-director of clinical research at the CTE Center at Boston University. And given the small sample size of the study, more research is needed to confirm the findings. But the results lay the groundwork for a blood test for CTE, he says.
paras.zh: 该研究的资深作者、波士顿大学 CTE 中心临床研究联席主任迈克尔·阿洛斯科 (Michael Alosco) 警告说，该测试尚未获得美国食品和药物管理局的批准。鉴于该研究的样本量较小，需要更多的研究来证实研究结果。但他说，结果为 CTE 血液检测奠定了基础。

paras.en: “If this finding holds up with future research, it opens up a lot of doors,” Alosco says. Researchers don’t know, for instance, how common CTE is in the general population—a test could help answer that question. It could also lead to better designed clinical trials to test therapeutics for CTE in living people, he says.
paras.zh: “如果这一发现适用于未来的研究，它将打开很多大门，”阿洛斯科说。例如，研究人员不知道 CTE 在普通人群中有多常见——一项测试可以帮助回答这个问题。他说，这还可能导致设计更好的临床试验来测试活人 CTE 的治疗方法。

paras.en: “We still have more work to do before you can bring it back to patients,” Alosco says. “But it’s an exciting first step.”
paras.zh: “在将其带回给患者之前，我们还有更多工作要做，”阿洛斯科说。 “但这是令人兴奋的第一步。”

paras.en: The test works by picking up on a biomarker for CTE related to specific protein clusters in the brain: Like Alzheimer’s disease, CTE is characterized by an “abnormality” in tau protein, Alosco explains. The protein “misfolds,” tangling and accumulating in brain cells. A biological signature, or biomarker—called endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau, or eMTBR-tau—can help detect those tangles, he says.
paras.zh: 该测试的工作原理是选取与大脑中特定蛋白质簇相关的 CTE 生物标志物：与阿尔茨海默病一样，CTE 的特点是 tau 蛋白的“异常”，Alosco 解释道。这种蛋白质“错误折叠”，在脑细胞中缠结并积聚。他说，生物特征或生物标志物（称为内源性裂解微管结合区 tau 或 eMTBR-tau）可以帮助检测这些缠结。

paras.en: This biomarker is elevated in people with both CTE and Alzheimer’s, so further testing is needed to “detect and differentiate” between diseases, he adds. That’s where another biomarker, called p-tau217, comes in: it is known to “track closely” with Alzheimer’s—but not with CTE, Alosco says. In theory, a two-part blood test for both biomarkers could identify patients with CTE.
paras.zh: 他补充说，这种生物标志物在患有 CTE 和阿尔茨海默病的人中都会升高，因此需要进一步的测试来“检测和区分”疾病。这就是另一种生物标记物 p-tau217 的用武之地：众所周知，它与阿尔茨海默氏症“密切相关”，但与 CTE 无关，阿洛斯科说。理论上，对两种生物标志物进行两部分血液检测可以识别 CTE 患者。

paras.en: The study comes days after the publication of another paper, also in JAMA, in which researchers using mass spectrometry found that eMTBR-tau was elevated in patients with severe cases of tau-related diseases, including Alzheimer’s and CTE.
paras.zh: 这项研究是在另一篇论文发表几天后发表的，该论文也在《美国医学会杂志》上发表，其中研究人员使用质谱法发现，患有严重 tau 相关疾病（包括阿尔茨海默病和 CTE）的患者中 eMTBR-tau 水平升高。

paras.en: “It is a watershed moment for the field, demonstrating that fluid biomarkers can work in assisting diagnosis of CTE in the living,” says Michael Buckland, a clinical associate professor of pathology at the University of Sydney in Australia, who was not involved in either new study. “A confident CTE diagnosis in the living opens the door for clinical trials to start finding treatments for the disease.”
paras.zh: 澳大利亚悉尼大学病理学临床副教授迈克尔·巴克兰（Michael Buckland）没有参与这两项新研究，他说：“这是该领域的一个分水岭，表明液体生物标志物可以帮助诊断活体 CTE。” “在活体中进行可靠的 CTE 诊断为临床试验打开了大门，以开始寻找该疾病的治疗方法。”

paras.en: “While there is still a long way to go before the test can be validated for clinical use, it is remarkable to see how fast the field is moving,” Buckland says.
paras.zh: 巴克兰说：“虽然该测试在临床应用验证之前还有很长的路要走，但该领域的发展速度令人瞩目。”

articles.title: We’ve been wrong about how language is produced in the brain for 150 years

paras.en: Scientists have spent centuries studying how humans produce language. A crucial early discovery was that there are two distinct language areas in the brain: one for listening and the other for speaking. These two regions, named Wernicke’s and Broca’s areas, after the 19th-century doctors who discovered them, are so fundamental to the science of language in the brain that they usually appear in the first chapter of textbooks on the subject.
paras.zh: 科学家们花了几个世纪的时间研究人类如何产生语言。一项重要的早期发现是，大脑中有两个不同的语言区域：一个负责听，另一个负责说。这两个区域被命名为韦尼克区和布罗卡区，以 19 世纪发现它们的医生的名字命名，它们对于大脑语言科学至关重要，因此通常出现在该主题教科书的第一章中。

paras.en: Those textbooks need to be rewritten. A new discovery, published today in Science, resolves a paradox that was first laid out by the eponymous physician Carl Wernicke himself by showing that Wernicke’s area, classically thought of as responsible only for speech perception, is actually responsible for language production as well.
paras.zh: 这些教科书需要重写。今天发表在《科学》杂志上的一项新发现解决了同名医生卡尔·韦尼克本人首次提出的一个悖论，该发现表明，传统上认为只负责言语感知的韦尼克区实际上也负责语言的产生。

paras.en: It’s “an amazing achievement” of neuroscience as a whole, said John Jay Ngai, the director of the National Institutes of Health’s BRAIN Initiative, at a press briefing during the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience this week. These findings “have really shown a much more complex [brain] structure than we had previously appreciated.”
paras.zh: 美国国立卫生研究院大脑计划主任 John Jay Ngai 在本周神经科学学会年会期间的新闻发布会上表示，这是整个神经科学领域的“一项惊人成就”。这些发现“确实显示出比我们之前想象的要复杂得多的[大脑]结构。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: In Wernicke’s day, neuroscientists learned what brain regions did by studying what happened when they were destroyed. Wernicke and his contemporary, physician Paul Broca, treated people with language disorders called aphasia. Broca noticed that patients who could barely produce speech at all had damage to a small region of their frontal lobe, located near the temple.
paras.zh: 在韦尼克时代，神经科学家通过研究大脑区域被破坏时发生的情况来了解大脑区域的功能。韦尼克和他同时代的医生保罗·布罗卡（Paul Broca）治疗了患有失语症的语言障碍患者。布罗卡注意到，那些几乎无法说话的患者，其额叶靠近太阳穴的一小部分区域受到了损伤。

paras.en: Conversely, some of Wernicke’s patients could speak fluidly but couldn’t understand the speech of others. They had damage to a region at the top of the temporal lobe, the auditory center of the brain, located above the ear. Wernicke theorized it was responsible for language production.
paras.zh: 相反，韦尼克的一些患者可以流利地说话，但无法理解其他人的讲话。他们的颞叶顶部区域受损，该区域是大脑的听觉中心，位于耳朵上方。韦尼克认为它负责语言的产生。

paras.en: But Wernicke’s patients, while producing fluent speech, did not necessarily speak well. They often produced nonsensical speech, sometimes described as “word salad.”
paras.zh: 但韦尼克的病人虽然能说流利的语言，但不一定说得很好。他们经常发表无意义的言论，有时被称为“言语沙拉”。

paras.en: It was a paradox: Why would damaging the language comprehension part of the brain prevent people from speaking clearly? Neuroscientists have theorized that this activity happened after people spoke—a sort of self-monitoring system that listened to their own speech. But the timescales involved are extremely short, and neuroscientists’ go-to method for noninvasive brain scanning, functional magnetic resonance imaging, operates too slowly to reveal this order of events.
paras.zh: 这是一个悖论：为什么损害大脑的语言理解部分会阻止人们清晰地说话？神经科学家推测，这种活动发生在人们说话之后——一种倾听自己讲话的自我监控系统。但所涉及的时间尺度非常短，神经科学家常用的无创脑部扫描方法——功能性磁共振成像——运行速度太慢，无法揭示事件的顺序。

paras.en: To figure out what was actually happening in Wernicke’s area while people speak, Edward Chang, a neurosurgeon at the University of California, San Francisco, and his colleagues recruited people undergoing brain surgery for epilepsy, who would remain awake during the procedure. Using an array of electric sensors placed directly on participants’ brains, the researchers measured activity in the organs’ language centers as the participants repeated and listened to words and sentences.
paras.zh: 为了弄清楚人们说话时韦尼克区到底发生了什么，旧金山加利福尼亚大学的神经外科医生爱德华·张和他的同事招募了接受癫痫脑部手术的人，这些人在手术过程中保持清醒。研究人员使用直接放置在参与者大脑上的一系列电传感器，测量了参与者重复和聆听单词和句子时器官语言中心的活动。

paras.en: “What we saw was not what the textbook predicted,” said Chang, the new study’s senior author, at a separate press briefing ahead of the study’s publication. A part of Wernicke’s area roughly the size of a nickel activated before people spoke. The amount of activity increased with the length of the word they were about to say. It also activated more when people said uncommon words. The researchers call this area the left posterior superior temporal gyrus, or lpSTG.
paras.zh: “What we saw was not what the textbook predicted,” said Chang, the new study’s senior author, at a separate press briefing ahead of the study’s publication.在人们说话之前，韦尼克区域的一部分大约有镍币大小。活动量随着他们要说的话的长度而增加。当人们说出不常见的词语时，它也会更加活跃。研究人员将该区域称为左后颞上回，或 lpSTG。

paras.en: “This is really an ‘auditory image’ of the sounds in the word that you’re planning to say,” said the study’s lead author Alexander Silva, a medical researcher at U.C. San Francisco, at the same briefing.
paras.zh: 该研究的主要作者、加州大学伯克利分校的医学研究员亚历山大·席尔瓦（Alexander Silva）说：“这实际上是你打算说的单词中声音的‘听觉图像’。”旧金山，在同一次新闻发布会上。

paras.en: Even more extraordinary, that same region—in fact, the exact same neurons—also activated while people listened to speech. “That really sort of struck me,” said study co-author Matthew Leonard, a cognitive neuroscientist at U.C. San Francisco, at the briefing. Scientists should start to question the long-standing idea that production and perception of speech are separate processes in the brain, he added. “They really do seem to be fully integrated.”
paras.zh: 更不同寻常的是，当人们听讲话时，同一区域（实际上是完全相同的神经元）也会激活。 “这确实让我震惊，”该研究的合著者、加州大学认知神经科学家马修·伦纳德 (Matthew Leonard) 说。旧金山，在新闻发布会上。他补充说，科学家应该开始质疑长期以来的观点，即言语的产生和感知是大脑中独立的过程。 “他们看起来确实完全融为一体了。”

paras.en: The researchers found that the lpSTG sends the signals it generates prior to speech straight to the motor centers of the brain, where they’re turned into muscle impulses that instruct our vocal tract to move. This was previously thought to be the job of Broca’s area in the more frontal parts of the brain that coordinate higher-level planning.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，lpSTG 在说话之前将其产生的信号直接发送到大脑的运动中心，在那里这些信号转化为肌肉冲动，指示我们的声道移动。此前人们认为这是布罗卡区的工作，该区域位于大脑的额叶部分，负责协调更高级别的计划。

paras.en: This new understanding of how we produce speech could be used to create brain-computer interfaces, or BCIs, to help people with brain damage communicate. Most BCIs are tested in people with paralysis who can no longer speak because of motor problems. These BCIs read out signals from the brain’s motor areas, the last stop before intended speech gets sent to the muscles.
paras.zh: 这种对我们如何产生语音的新理解可用于创建脑机接口（BCI），以帮助脑损伤患者进行交流。大多数脑机接口都是在因运动问题而无法说话的瘫痪患者身上进行测试的。这些脑机接口读取来自大脑运动区域的信号，这是将想要的语音发送到肌肉之前的最后一站。

paras.en: But for people with aphasia, intended speech usually doesn’t make it to the motor centers intact. BCIs that work for them would need to decode what they intend to say from the activation of upstream language planning areas. Pinpointing these areas could lead to neuroprostheses for these conditions.
paras.zh: 但对于失语症患者来说，有意的言语通常无法完好无损地到达运动中枢。为他们工作的脑机接口需要从上游语言规划区域的激活中解码他们想要说的话。精确定位这些区域可能会导致针对这些情况的神经假体的出现。

paras.en: All of this, however, suddenly leaves the role of Broca’s area unclear. “If both during language comprehension and during language production, the main ‘action’ is happening in the temporal lobe..., why do we have the frontal-lobe components of the language network?” says Evelina Fedorenko, a cognitive neuroscientist, who studies language at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and was not involved in the new research.
paras.zh: All of this, however, suddenly leaves the role of Broca’s area unclear. “如果在语言理解和语言产生过程中，主要的‘动作’都发生在颞叶......，为什么我们有语言网络的额叶组件？”在麻省理工学院研究语言的认知神经科学家 Evelina Fedorenko 表示，她没有参与这项新研究。

paras.en: Broca’s area “is still clearly important,” Leonard said. “In some ways, it's sort of the next mystery.”
paras.zh: 伦纳德说，布罗卡的区域“显然仍然很重要”。 “从某种程度上来说，这就是下一个谜团。”

articles.title: Voyager 1 is a light-day away. What now?

paras.en: On Thursday, at around 5 A.M. EST, while we all slept on our “Pale Blue Dot,” scientists at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) received a signal from Voyager 1 confirming it had indeed reached one light-day, around 16 billion miles, away from Earth. Technically, Voyager hit the distance on Wednesday, but because it is so far away, communications between it and Earth are delayed.
paras.zh: 周四早上 5 点左右美国东部时间，当我们都睡在“淡蓝点”上时，美国宇航局喷气推进实验室 (JPL) 的科学家们收到了航海家 1 号的信号，确认它确实已经到达一光日，距离地球约 160 亿英里。从技术上讲，航行者号于周三到达了这一距离，但由于距离太远，它与地球之间的通信出现了延迟。

paras.en: Voyager 1’s milestone, the farthest any human-made object has ever been from Earth, comes after almost half a century worth of solar system exploration alongside its sister spacecraft Voyager 2. They were both launched in 1977 to explore the outer solar system and the limits of the sun’s influence.
paras.zh: 航海者 1 号的里程碑是迄今为止距离地球最远的人造物体，它是在与其姊妹航天器航海者 2 号一起进行了近半个世纪的太阳系探索之后实现的。它们均于 1977 年发射，旨在探索外太阳系和太阳影响的极限。

paras.en: “My hope is that Voyager, just as it was inspirational to us, is inspirational to the next generation,” said Suzanne Dodd, NASA’s Voyager project manager, at a press conference on Thursday. “One light-day is a great milestone, but I think we’re going to have more milestones to come.”
paras.zh: “我希望 Voyager 不仅能激励我们，还能激励下一代，”美国宇航局 Voyager 项目经理苏珊娜·多德 (Suzanne Dodd) 在周四的新闻发布会上说道。 “一个光日是一个伟大的里程碑，但我认为我们还会有更多的里程碑。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: In its lifetime, the Voyager mission has provided insights into Saturn, Jupiter, Neptune, Uranus, and more. Now its legacy is informing missions such as the Europa Clipper, which is expected to arrive at Jupiter in 2030 to study the planet’s icy moon Europa. We would know nearly nothing about Europa if not for Voyager. The same goes for Dragonfly, a mission launching in 2028 to explore Titan, Saturn’s largest moon.
paras.zh: 在其一生中，航海家号任务提供了对土星、木星、海王星、天王星等的深入了解。现在，它的遗产正在为木卫二快艇等任务提供信息，该快艇预计将于 2030 年抵达木星，研究木星的冰冷卫星木卫二。如果没有航行者号，我们对木卫二几乎一无所知。蜻蜓号也是如此，该任务于 2028 年发射，旨在探索土星最大的卫星泰坦。

paras.en: “The discoveries of Voyager really opened the door to the outer solar system,” said JPL chief scientist Jonathan Lunine at the same press event.
paras.zh: 喷气推进实验室首席科学家乔纳森·卢宁在同一次新闻发布会上表示：“航行者号的发现确实打开了通往外太阳系的大门。”

paras.en: As for the Voyager spacecraft themselves, each data point we receive from them now is “precious” and unprecedented, said Nicky Fox, associate administrator at NASA’s Science Mission Directorate. Both Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 are in interstellar space, or the area between our solar system and others, and are collecting data with their active instruments about how our sun influences this in-between place. Both spacecraft have tools that measure plasma waves and magnetic fields, as well as a system that measures cosmic rays.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局科学任务理事会副局长尼基·福克斯表示，就航海者号航天器本身而言，我们现在从它们那里收到的每个数据点都是“珍贵的”且前所未有的。航海者 1 号和航海者 2 号都位于星际空间，即我们的太阳系和其他太阳系之间的区域，并且正在使用其主动仪器收集有关我们的太阳如何影响这个中间位置的数据。这两艘航天器都有测量等离子体波和磁场的工具，以及测量宇宙射线的系统。

paras.en: “We’re at a very exciting time of starting to connect what we know and what we’ve seen living with this star to what is out there,” said Jamie Rankin, Voyager deputy project scientist.
paras.zh: 航行者号副项目科学家杰米·兰金 (Jamie Rankin) 表示：“我们正处于一个非常激动人心的时刻，开始将我们所知道的以及我们所看到的与这颗恒星一起生活的事物与那里的事物联系起来。”

paras.en: At nearly 50 years old, the spacecraft are aging gracefully—but aging nonetheless. As of a few days ago, NASA has not been able to receive scientific data from Voyager 1. And earlier this year the team chose to shut down several power-hungry devices on both spacecraft to conserve energy. Much of the team’s current work involves confronting and finding solutions for nearly constant new anomalies, said Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager.
paras.zh: 航天器已有近 50 年的历史，它正在优雅地老化——但仍然在老化。截至几天前，美国宇航局还无法接收航行者一号的科学数据。今年早些时候，该团队选择关闭两艘航天器上的几个耗电设备以节省能源。航行者号任务经理卡里姆·巴达鲁丁 (Kareem Badaruddin) 表示，该团队目前的大部分工作涉及面对几乎不断出现的新异常现象并寻找解决方案。

paras.en: “An engineer with a problem is like a dog with a bone, so we are very busy and very energized to solve these problems,” he said.
paras.zh: “工程师遇到问题就像狗遇到骨头，所以我们非常忙碌，也非常有精力去解决这些问题，”他说。

paras.en: Voyager 1 is expected to lose power in 2036, at which point it will no longer communicate with Earth. But it will keep shooting through space. Set for a destination of 17 light-years away, it carries a “Golden Record”—a history of Earth and humanity meant for any extraterrestrial life the spacecraft may encounter.
paras.zh: Voyager 1 is expected to lose power in 2036, at which point it will no longer communicate with Earth. But it will keep shooting through space.它的目的地是 17 光年外，它承载着一份“黄金记录”——地球和人类的历史，适用于航天器可能遇到的任何外星生命。

paras.en: “There’s no end for the Voyager mission,” Fox said.
paras.zh: “航行者号的任务永无止境，”福克斯说。

articles.title: American science is broken. Meet the people fixing it
articles.author: Hannah Richter

paras.en: The February sun was setting outside her family’s West Virginia home when Rebecca Lindsey found out she was being fired in 75 minutes. Lindsey, who until early 2025 managed the federal government’s climate.gov website, had just begun to think her job might be safe during the second Trump administration.
paras.zh: 当丽贝卡·林赛 (Rebecca Lindsey) 75 分钟后发现自己将被解雇时，二月的太阳正在她位于西弗吉尼亚州的家外落下。林赛在 2025 年初之前一直负责管理联邦政府的 Climate.gov 网站，她刚刚开始认为在特朗普第二届政府期间她的工作可能会很安全。

paras.en: “Every week, it was like, ‘This is the week we’re all going to get fired,’ ” says Lindsey, who had worked as a contractor and later a civil servant at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration for nearly 15 years. “Every time you would hear the rumor and then it wouldn’t happen, you would think … maybe this is all just talk.”
paras.zh: “每一周，我们都会感觉‘这周我们都会被解雇’，”林赛说，他曾在国家海洋和大气管理局担任承包商，后来担任公务员近 15 年。 “每次你听到谣言，然后这件事并没有发生，你就会想……也许这只是说说而已。”

paras.en: But at 3:45 p.m. on February 27, 2025, Lindsey and around 800 of her NOAA colleagues received a mass termination email saying they no longer “fit the Agency’s current needs.” In June, Lindsey’s sister and the data visualization lead for the project, Mary Lindsey, was fired alongside the remaining climate.gov contractors. The website URL was redirected, hiding the site — and its decades’ worth of climate visualizations, educational tools and extreme weather trackers — from the public.
paras.zh: 但下午 3 点 45 分2025 年 2 月 27 日，Lindsey 和约 800 名 NOAA 同事收到一封大规模解雇电子邮件，称他们不再“符合该机构当前的需求”。六月，Lindsey 的妹妹兼该项目的数据可视化负责人 Mary Lindsey 与其余的 Climate.gov 承包商一起被解雇。该网站的 URL 被重定向，向公众隐藏了该网站及其数十年的气候可视化、教育工具和极端天气跟踪器。

paras.en: The Lindsey sisters decided to fight back. Along with another terminated NOAA employee, they split a $65,000 grant from the nonprofit Surge Climate Talent and launched a crowdfunding campaign to rebuild and update climate.gov. The site, now called climate.us, notched one million views in its first month.
paras.zh: 林赛姐妹决定反击。他们与另一名被 NOAA 解雇的员工一起，分享了非营利组织 Surge Climate Talent 提供的 65,000 美元赠款，并发起了一项众筹活动，以重建和更新 Climate.gov。该网站现名为 Climate.us，上线第一个月就获得了 100 万次浏览量。

paras.en: But as proud as they are of their work, the project is a patch, not a fix.
