Kennedy, whose department oversees the CDC, is a longtime vaccine skeptic. O’Neill is widely considered a key Kennedy ally and a proponent of the “Make America Healthy Again” movement. Many science advocates and organizations such as a the Union of Concerned Scientists had campaigned against his nomination, citing his actions during his time as acting CDC director and his background in biotechnology investment as reasons he should not be considered for the job.
paras.zh: 莫纳雷斯于 2025 年被解除 CDC 主任职务，她将此归咎于她拒绝批准缺乏证据的疫苗建议或无故解雇机构员工。肯尼迪领导的疾病预防控制中心部门长期以来一直对疫苗持怀疑态度。奥尼尔被广泛认为是肯尼迪的重要盟友和“让美国再次健康”运动的支持者。许多科学倡导者和忧思科学家联盟等组织反对他的提名，称他在担任疾病预防控制中心代理主任期间的行为以及他在生物技术投资方面的背景是他不应该被考虑担任这一职位的原因。

paras.en: The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while a spokesperson for the NSF declined to comment.
paras.zh: 白宫没有立即回应置评请求，国家科学基金会发言人也拒绝置评。

paras.en: In a post on X in the wake of Overton’s removal, Cassidy said she had a “viable confirmation path,” but the White House did not believe she had the votes.
paras.zh: 奥弗顿被免职后，卡西迪在 X 上发帖称，她有“可行的确认途径”，但白宫不相信她拥有选票。

paras.en: “This was odd as I was having productive conversations with members,” Cassidy wrote. “I believe she would have had the votes to pass out of committee and pass the full Senate. My conversations with her convinced me she would follow the science and push back against decisions that put Americans’ health at risk.”
paras.zh: “这很奇怪，因为我正在与成员进行富有成效的对话，”卡西迪写道。 “我相信她会获得委员会的选票，并在参议院获得通过。我与她的谈话使我相信，她会遵循科学，反对那些将美国人的健康置于危险之中的决定。”

paras.en: Cassidy alleged that the only issue that stood in the way of Overton’s confirmation was that antiabortion senators had sought assurances from the White House that the FDA would back their agenda.
paras.zh: 卡西迪声称，阻碍奥弗顿确认的唯一问题是反堕胎参议员已寻求白宫保证 FDA 将支持他们的议程。

paras.en: “The Administration withdrew Dr. Overton rather than make such commitments,” he wrote. “Unfortunately, with the limited time left, confirming a permanent FDA Commissioner will fall to Senate Democrats.”
paras.zh: “政府没有做出这样的承诺，而是撤回了奥弗顿博士，”他写道。 “不幸的是，在剩下的时间有限的情况下，确认 FDA 常任专员将落在参议院民主党人的手中。”

paras.en: Although Overton had praised Trump during her confirmation hearing in September, she also distanced herself from some of his more outlandish positions, telling the committee that Tylenol use during pregnancy has not been found to cause autism and that the mumps, measles and rubella (MMR) vaccine is safe and effective. She also said the abortion drug mifepristone met FDA safety and efficacy standards. The drug has been at the center of legal efforts to reduce abortion access, with antiabortion proponents falsely claiming the drug is unsafe.
paras.zh: 尽管奥弗顿在 9 月份的确认听证会上赞扬了特朗普，但她也与特朗普的一些更古怪的立场保持了距离，她告诉委员会，尚未发现怀孕期间使用泰诺会导致自闭症，而且腮腺炎、麻疹和风疹 (MMR) 疫苗是安全有效的。她还表示，堕胎药物米非司酮符合 FDA 的安全性和有效性标准。该药物一直是减少堕胎机会的法律努力的核心，反堕胎支持者错误地声称该药物不安全。

paras.en: Editor’s Note (11/18/26): This is a breaking news story and may be updated.
paras.zh: 编者注（11/18/26）：这是一个突发新闻报道，可能会更新。

articles.title: Ancient fossils reveal Homo erectus survived in China some 200,000 years longer than we thought

paras.en: The ancient human Homo erectus emerged nearly two million years ago and spread from Africa to as far as the Indonesian island of Java. Now fossils discovered in two caves in southern China are helping to color in parts of this ancient human ancestor’s journey. By analyzing the fossils, researchers have found that H. erectus survived on the Asian mainland for around 200,000 years longer than we previously thought. And it did so in dense rainforest, long considered the particular domain of Homo sapiens.
paras.zh: 古代人类直立人出现在近两百万年前，并从非洲传播到印度尼西亚爪哇岛。现在，在中国南方的两个洞穴中发现的化石正在为这位古代人类祖先的部分旅程增添色彩。通过分析化石，研究人员发现直立人在亚洲大陆的生存时间比我们之前想象的要长约20万年。它是在茂密的雨林中进行的，长期以来，这里被认为是智人的特殊领域。

paras.en: The conclusions, published in two new studies in Nature, run contrary to assumptions, based on past fossil finds, that H. erectus was a specialist species that preferred grass and woodlands and that struggled to adapt to different habitats. Before these new discoveries, scientists had found no securely dated fossils younger than about 400,000 years on the Asian mainland. The last known members of the species lived on Java until about 110,000 years ago, and encroaching rainforests have been blamed for their extinction.
paras.zh: 这项结论发表在《自然》杂志上的两项新研究中，与基于过去化石发现的假设相反，即直立人是一种喜欢草地和林地并且难以适应不同栖息地的特殊物种。在这些新发现之前，科学家们在亚洲大陆尚未发现任何年龄小于 40 万年的化石。该物种最后已知的成员生活在爪哇，直到大约 11 万年前，雨林的入侵被认为是它们灭绝的原因。

paras.en: “The idea never really sat very well with me,” says Kira Westaway, a geochronologist at Macquarie University in Australia, who co-led one of the studies. H. erectus, she explains, survived for a really long time, which made her doubt the species lacked the flexibility to live in different environments.
paras.zh: 其中一项研究的共同领导者、澳大利亚麦考瑞大学的地质年代学家基拉·韦斯特韦 (Kira Westaway) 表示：“我从来没有真正接受过这个想法。”她解释说，直立人存活了很长一段时间，这让她怀疑该物种缺乏在不同环境中生活的灵活性。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Westaway’s team dated the fossil-bearing layers of China’s Naxian Cave and Baxian Cave with five independent methods, placing the H. erectus fossils there sometime between 324,000 and 184,000 years ago. Carbon isotopes in the enamel of animal teeth at the sites showed that animals in the caves fed exclusively in the closed-canopy forest that once surround them. And H. erectus teeth that were also found there carried similar signatures. This suggests these ancient people were not just passing through the rainforest but lived there.
paras.zh: Westaway 的团队用五种独立的方法对中国纳仙洞和八仙洞的化石层进行了年代测定，将直立人化石放置在距今 324,000 至 184,000 年前的某个时间。这些遗址的动物牙釉质中的碳同位素表明，洞穴中的动物只在曾经围绕它们的封闭树冠森林中进食。在那里发现的直立人牙齿也带有类似的特征。这表明这些古人不仅经过雨林，而且还居住在那里。

paras.en: H. erectus also appears to have been a keen traveler. The teeth contain strontium, an element taken up from food and water whose chemical signature reflects the underlying rock. In the H. erectus teeth, the signature didn’t match the local limestone, suggesting these individuals traveled a lot, possibly from as far as northern Vietnam, some 250 kilometers away.
paras.zh: 直立人似乎也是一位热衷于旅行的人。这些牙齿含有锶，这是一种从食物和水中吸收的元素，其化学特征反映了下面的岩石。直立人牙齿上的特征与当地的石灰岩不符，表明这些人经常旅行，可能远至约 250 公里外的越南北部。

paras.en: “This emphasizes that behavioral flexibility was likely a key to Homo erectus success, both in terms of the long duration of the species and its broad dispersal,” says Susan Antón, a paleoanthropologist at New York University, who was not involved in the new research.
paras.zh: 纽约大学古人类学家苏珊·安东（未参与这项新研究）表示：“这强调了行为灵活性可能是直立人成功的关键，无论是从该物种的长期存在还是其广泛的传播来看。”

paras.en: In the other Nature study, a second team extracted ancient proteins from the tooth enamel.
paras.zh: 在《自然》杂志的另一项研究中，第二个团队从牙釉质中提取了古老的蛋白质。

paras.en: “Proteins, especially skeletal proteins, fall apart inherently slower than ancient DNA does,” says Frido Welker, a molecular anthropologist at the University of Copenhagen and senior author of the study. Four teeth carried a version of the enamel protein ameloblastin, which had only been seen in older H. erectus fossils found in China, but they lacked another variant those fossils share. Welker’s team interpreted that as a clue that the newly analyzed teeth belonged to a previously unknown lineage of H. erectus.
paras.zh: “蛋白质，尤其是骨骼蛋白，本质上分解的速度比古代 DNA 慢，”哥本哈根大学分子人类学家、该研究的资深作者 Frido Welker 说。四颗牙齿携带一种牙釉质蛋白成釉细胞蛋白，这种蛋白只在中国发现的较古老的直立人化石中发现过，但它们缺乏这些化石所共有的另一种变体。韦尔克的团队将此解释为一条线索，表明新分析的牙齿属于以前未知的直立人谱系。

paras.en: “I appreciated how Welker and his colleagues came to the conclusion that they were looking at a novel Homo erectus lineage,” says Sheela Athreya, a paleoanthropologist at Texas A&M University, who was not involved in either study. “I would not be surprised if these results are confirmed by other studies.”
paras.zh: “我很欣赏韦尔克和他的同事们得出的结论，他们正在研究一种新的直立人谱系，”德克萨斯农工大学的古人类学家希拉·阿瑟雷亚（Sheela Athreya）说，她没有参与这两项研究。 “如果这些结果得到其他研究的证实，我不会感到惊讶。”

paras.en: One unsolved mystery from the new research is that another hominin tooth found in the Baxian cave fit neither H. erectus nor Neanderthals nor modern humans. “I think Denisovans would be the first option to consider,” Welker says. He cautions, however, that no comparable Denisovan tooth exists to check against and that proteins hold far less concrete information than DNA.
paras.zh: 这项新研究中的一个未解之谜是，在巴仙洞穴中发现的另一颗古人类牙齿既不适合直立人，也不适合尼安德特人，也不适合现代人类。 “我认为丹尼索瓦人将是第一个考虑的选择，”韦尔克说。然而，他警告说，不存在可比的丹尼索瓦人牙齿可供对照，而且蛋白质所包含的具体信息远不如DNA。

paras.en: “This is important because these hominins could have been related to Denisovans that already inhabited Asia or even Neanderthals in Europe,” says Karen Baab, a paleoanthropologist at Midwestern University in Arizona, who was not involved in the new research. “I hope there will be future fossils from southern China that can help confirm this species diagnosis.”
paras.zh: “这很重要，因为这些古人类可能与已经居住在亚洲的丹尼索瓦人甚至欧洲的尼安德特人有关，”亚利桑那州中西部大学的古人类学家凯伦·巴布（Karen Baab）说，她没有参与这项新研究。 “我希望未来有来自中国南方的化石可以帮助确认这个物种的诊断。”

paras.en: The search for such new fossils, Westaway says, is already ongoing. Her team returns to China every year, with cavers exploring four or five caves a day. “There’s a lot to be done,” she says.
paras.zh: 韦斯特韦说，对此类新化石的搜寻工作已经在进行中。她的团队每年都会回到中国，探洞者每天探索四到五个洞穴。 “还有很多事情要做，”她说。

articles.title: The brain’s fear center moonlights as the save button for memories
articles.author: Allie Skalnik

paras.en: The walnut-sized fear center of the brain also distinguishes the memorable from the mundane.
paras.zh: 大脑核桃大小的恐惧中心也将难忘的事情与平凡的事情区分开来。

paras.en: Neurons in the amygdala act like a save button for memories, scientists report October 27 in Nature Neuroscience. Though the study doesn’t nail down the exact mechanism for memory formation, it points to a broader role for the amygdala within the memory-sorting apparatus.
paras.zh: 科学家于 10 月 27 日在《自然神经科学》杂志上发表报告称，杏仁核中的神经元就像记忆的保存按钮。尽管这项研究没有确定记忆形成的确切机制，但它指出了杏仁核在记忆分类装置中发挥着更广泛的作用。

paras.en: The study probes an enduring quandary about the mind, says neuroscientist Jiayang Xiao of Cedars-Sinai Health Sciences University in Los Angeles. “We forget much of what we experience … only a fraction of the information we encounter becomes a lasting memory,” she says.
paras.zh: 洛杉矶雪松-西奈健康科学大学的神经科学家肖嘉阳表示，这项研究探讨了关于大脑的一个持久的难题。 “我们忘记了我们经历过的很多事情……只有我们遇到的信息的一小部分会成为持久的记忆，”她说。

paras.en: Although a role for the amygdala in memory has been suggested before, previous studies that used electrodes reading brain activity through the scalp, or at the scale of thousands rather than individual neurons, captured a blurrier picture. It’s akin to a microphone recording from outside of a stadium, says cognitive neuroscientist Cory Inman at the University of Utah in Salt Lake City, who was not involved in the study.
paras.zh: 尽管之前已经提出过杏仁核在记忆中的作用，但之前的研究使用电极通过头皮读取大脑活动，或者以数千个而不是单个神经元的规模读取大脑活动，捕捉到的图像更加模糊。盐湖城犹他大学认知神经科学家科里·英曼（未参与这项研究）表示，这类似于体育场外的麦克风录音。

paras.en: “You might be able to tell that there’s a game happening. You might be able to tell when somebody scores a touchdown. You might even be able to tell that one side of the stadium is cheering for one team and another side of the stadium is cheering for another team,” but that’s about it, Inman says. The new study is more like a lapel mic pinned on a single fan in terms of scale and what the researchers were able to capture, adding clarity.
paras.zh: “你也许能够分辨出正在发生一场比赛。你也许能够分辨出某人何时达阵。你甚至可能能够分辨出体育场的一侧正在为一支球队欢呼，而体育场的另一侧正在为另一支球队欢呼，”但仅此而已，英曼说。就规模和研究人员能够捕获的内容而言，这项新研究更像是固定在单个风扇上的翻领麦克风，从而增加了清晰度。

paras.en: The amygdala, which is typically associated with regulating emotions like fear and aggression, has neurons that are challenging to reach, residing in two clusters deep within the brain. Xiao and her colleagues leveraged electrodes previously surgically implanted in more than 90 people with drug-resistant epilepsy to identify where seizures originate. In their new role, the electrodes singled out neurons involved in saving memories.
paras.zh: 杏仁核通常与调节恐惧和攻击性等情绪有关，其神经元难以到达，位于大脑深处的两个簇中。肖和她的同事利用之前通过手术植入 90 多名耐药性癫痫患者体内的电极来确定癫痫发作的根源。在新的角色中，电极挑选出了参与保存记忆的神经元。

paras.en: Patients were shown images of everyday objects belonging to five categories such as food and animals. About 10 to 30 minutes later, they attempted to recall which images were already shown. Xiao and her colleagues found that activity in certain amygdala neurons corresponded with an image being remembered. The image had been earmarked for longer term storage, Xiao says.
paras.zh: 向患者展示属于食物和动物等五类的日常物品的图像。大约 10 到 30 分钟后，他们试图回忆起已经播放过哪些图像。肖和她的同事发现，某些杏仁核神经元的活动与所记住的图像相对应。肖说，该图像已指定用于长期存储。

paras.en: Although participants had to recall something from half an hour ago at most and the exact mechanism for saving memories is still unclear, the researchers think there are two main steps of the process. The team showed that individual neurons have a preference for one of the five categories of images. First the image is categorized by the amygdala. Then, the strength of the category neuron response the first time the image is shown dictates whether the image is later recalled.
paras.zh: 尽管参与者最多只能回忆半小时前的事情，而且保存记忆的确切机制仍不清楚，但研究人员认为这个过程有两个主要步骤。研究小组表明，单个神经元对五类图像之一有偏好。首先，图像按杏仁核分类。然后，第一次显示图像时类别神经元响应的强度决定了以后是否会回忆起该图像。

paras.en: A better understanding of this mechanism may pave the way for more effective treatments of memory disorders, Xiao says, a medical conundrum for which there are currently no broadly effective treatments.
paras.zh: 肖说，更好地理解这一机制可能为更有效地治疗记忆障碍铺平道路，这是一个目前还没有广泛有效的治疗方法的医学难题。

paras.en: The hippocampus is typically more directly linked to memory, so “it surprised me that we observe such a clear relationship between memory formation and activity in the amygdala,” Xiao says. By contrast, the correlation between hippocampus neuron activity and image recall was weaker and slightly delayed.
paras.zh: 海马体通常与记忆有更直接的联系，因此“令我惊讶的是，我们观察到记忆形成和杏仁核活动之间存在如此清晰的关系，”肖说。相比之下，海马神经元活动与图像回忆之间的相关性较弱且略有延迟。

paras.en: Future work like observing the impacts of stimulating amygdala neurons on memory will help researchers discern if this region can be targeted to improve memory, Xiao says.
paras.zh: 肖说，未来的工作，比如观察刺激杏仁核神经元对记忆的影响，将有助于研究人员辨别该区域是否可以针对改善记忆。

paras.en: For now, the secret to memory’s hidden machinations remains in the shadows.
paras.zh: 目前，记忆中隐藏的阴谋的秘密仍然处于阴影之中。

articles.title: Most transgender youth satisfied after choosing hormone therapy
articles.author: Aimee Cunningham

paras.en: An overwhelming percentage of transgender and gender diverse young people in the United States express satisfaction with gender-affirming hormone therapy.
paras.zh: 在美国，绝大多数跨性别和性别多样化的年轻人对性别肯定激素疗法表示满意。

paras.en: Almost 400 transgender and gender diverse young people reflected on their decision to take hormone therapy in the largest such survey to date. Nearly 97 percent affirmed it was the right decision, researchers report November 9 in JAMA Pediatrics. Only about 3 percent, or 10 individuals, said they regretted the step, and of those, seven felt the experience was harmful.
paras.zh: 在迄今为止最大规模的此类调查中，近 400 名跨性别和性别多样化的年轻人反思了他们接受激素治疗的决定。研究人员 11 月 9 日在《美国医学会儿科杂志》上发表报告称，近 97% 的人确认这是正确的决定。只有大约 3%（即 10 人）表示他们对这一步骤感到后悔，其中 7 人认为这种经历是有害的。

paras.en: With concerns around youth well-being fueling limits on gender-affirming hormone therapy, the researchers write, “the results provide further support for the existing standards of care [and] do not support efforts to categorically restrict or ban access.”
paras.zh: 研究人员写道，由于对青少年福祉的担忧加剧了对性别肯定激素疗法的限制，“研究结果为现有的护理标准提供了进一步的支持，[并且]不支持明确限制或禁止使用的努力。”

paras.en: Gender-affirming hormone therapy — with the masculinizing hormone testosterone or the feminizing hormone estrogen — allows a person’s body to better match their gender identity. Around 3 percent of 13- to 17-year-olds in the United States identify as transgender.
paras.zh: 性别肯定激素疗法——使用男性化激素睾酮或女性化激素雌激素——可以让一个人的身体更好地匹配他们的性别认同。在美国，大约 3% 的 13 至 17 岁青少年认为自己是跨性别者。

paras.en: Among the study’s 376 young people, who were former patients of a clinic for transgender and gender diverse youth, nearly 92 percent began hormones at 17 or younger. Thirty percent took estrogen and 70 percent took testosterone, with the amount of time since starting the hormones averaging five years.
paras.zh: 在该研究的 376 名年轻人中，近 92% 的人在 17 岁或更年轻时开始服用激素，这些人曾是跨性别和性别多元化青少年诊所的患者。 30% 的人服用雌激素，70% 的人服用睾酮，距离开始使用激素的时间平均为五年。

paras.en: As per clinical guidelines for transgender health care, young people interested in medical treatment, joined by parents or guardians, began with an assessment visit with a mental health professional. For the study, participants took a yearly survey, filled out anytime from one month prior to six months following the anniversary of this initial visit. The research team analyzed surveys submitted from 2023 to 2025.
paras.zh: 根据跨性别医疗保健的临床指南，对医疗感兴趣的年轻人在父母或监护人的陪同下，首先接受心理健康专业人士的评估访问。在这项研究中，参与者每年进行一次调查，并在首次访问周年纪念日后六个月内的任何时间填写。研究团队分析了 2023 年至 2025 年提交的调查。

paras.en: The new research adds to growing evidence on the benefits of gender-affirming hormone therapy for transgender young people. Gender-affirming hormones improve the alignment these young people experience between their appearance and their gender, increase their satisfaction with life and reduce depression and anxiety.
paras.zh: 这项新研究进一步证明了性别肯定激素疗法对跨性别年轻人的益处。性别肯定荷尔蒙可以改善这些年轻人的外表和性别之间的一致性，提高他们对生活的满意度，并减少抑郁和焦虑。

paras.en: But state bans have curtailed young people’s access to gender-affirming care, which can include hormone therapy and puberty blockers. As of November 2026 in the United States, 28 states have laws or policies that limit this care, according to the health policy organization KFF. More than half of transgender young people age 13 to 17 reside in states that restrict gender-affirming care. The American Academy of Pediatrics and the Endocrine Society support gender-affirming health care for young people and provide evidence-backed guidelines for treatment.
paras.zh: 但各州的禁令限制了年轻人获得性别肯定护理的机会，其中包括激素疗法和青春期阻滞剂。根据健康政策组织 KFF 的数据，截至 2026 年 11 月，美国有 28 个州制定了限制这种护理的法律或政策。超过一半的 13 至 17 岁跨性别年轻人居住在限制性别肯定护理的州。美国儿科学会和内分泌学会支持对年轻人进行性别肯定的医疗保健，并提供有证据支持的治疗指南。

articles.title: We know how to stop computer worms. But what if AI helps them persist?
articles.author: Kathryn Hulick

paras.en: AI is already powering new, more adaptable forms of cyberattack, but hackers typically wield the technology from afar. What if they set the AI models themselves loose to self-replicate and spread in a malicious manner?
paras.zh: 人工智能已经为新的、适应性更强的网络攻击形式提供了动力，但黑客通常会远程利用该技术。如果他们让人工智能模型自行自我复制并以恶意方式传播怎么办？

paras.en: Recent experiments have demonstrated two different ways this could happen. Two independent teams showed how a cyberattacker could turn an AI model into a “worm,” a type of malware that, unlike a computer virus, spreads on its own. And AI unlocked a new worm power: adapting attacks to different devices.
paras.zh: 最近的实验证明了这种情况可以通过两种不同的方式发生。两个独立团队展示了网络攻击者如何将人工智能模型变成“蠕虫”，这是一种恶意软件，与计算机病毒不同，它会自行传播。人工智能解锁了蠕虫病毒的新能力：使攻击适应不同的设备。

paras.en: The results hint at a new way AI could be used to ramp up cybersecurity threats — not just to computer systems but to smart devices such as security cameras or refrigerators. The good news is that the world still has time to build up defenses as several obstacles remain before this type of malware would work in the real world, says AI researcher Jonas Guan.
paras.zh: 研究结果暗示了人工智能可以用于增强网络安全威胁的新方式——不仅针对计算机系统，还针对安全摄像头或冰箱等智能设备。人工智能研究员 Jonasguan 表示，好消息是，世界仍然有时间建立防御措施，因为此类恶意软件在现实世界中发挥作用还存在一些障碍。

paras.en: AI could indeed make a worm “much harder to stop,” he says, but “there are a lot of kinks to iron out before something like this really works at scale.”
paras.zh: 他说，人工智能确实可以让蠕虫“更难阻止”，但“在这样的事情真正大规模发挥作用之前，还有很多问题需要解决。”

paras.en: Morphing simple worms into shrewd attackers
paras.zh: 将简单的蠕虫变成精明的攻击者

paras.en: Here is how a worm cyberattack works. A malware worm squirms through the internet, copying itself onto whatever systems it can hijack. Hackers can then mine hijacked systems directly for their data or link them together into a botnet and use its computing power, often to send spam email or overwhelm websites with traffic, knocking them offline.
paras.zh: 以下是蠕虫网络攻击的工作原理。恶意软件蠕虫在互联网中蠕动，将自身复制到它可以劫持的任何系统上。然后，黑客可以直接挖掘被劫持的系统以获取数据，或将它们链接到僵尸网络中并利用其计算能力，通常会发送垃圾邮件或淹没网站，导致其离线。

paras.en: Historically, computer worms have been small, simple programs preprogrammed to take advantage of specific security weaknesses. So they could only get into devices that had that weakness. When defenders patched a worm’s target, it could no longer spread. With an AI model directing its actions, however, a worm can adapt and learn on the fly, choosing its line of attack depending on the device, says Guan, of the University of Toronto.
paras.zh: 从历史上看，计算机蠕虫都是经过预先编程的小而简单的程序，以利用特定的安全弱点。所以他们只能进入有这个弱点的设备。当防御者修补了蠕虫的目标后，它就无法再传播。然而，多伦多大学的关说，有了人工智能模型指导其行动，蠕虫就可以动态适应和学习，根据设备选择攻击路线。

paras.en: That adaptability enables the worm to burrow into many different types of devices, both experiments showed. When hackers unleash AI from afar, they orchestrate what the model does. An AI worm that copies itself widely could hypothetically escape anyone’s control.
paras.zh: 两项实验都表明，这种适应性使蠕虫能够钻入许多不同类型的设备中。当黑客从远处释放人工智能时，他们会协调模型的行为。假设一种能够广泛复制自身的人工智能蠕虫可以逃脱任何人的控制。

paras.en: Still, there’s a caveat to the experiments’ results, says Michael Alexander Riegler, a cybersecurity researcher at Simula Metropolitan Center for Digital Engineering in Oslo, Norway. Both teams’ test environments made it easier for the AI worm to spread than it would be in the real world, says Riegler, who was not involved in either study.
paras.zh: 挪威奥斯陆 Simula 大都会数字工程中心的网络安全研究员迈克尔·亚历山大·里格勒 (Michael Alexander Riegler) 表示，实验结果仍然有一个警告。没有参与这两项研究的里格勒表示，两个团队的测试环境都使人工智能蠕虫病毒比在现实世界中更容易传播。

paras.en: And there’s another practical obstacle to the unleashing of AI worms. They use more computing power and take up more space than a conventional worm. The Mirai worm, which took down a slew of websites including Reddit and Spotify in 2016, was a few kilobytes in size, while the medium-sized AI models in the experiments were tens of gigabytes. That’s still way smaller than the massive, top-of-the-line models behind the “rogue AI” incidents that made headlines earlier in 2026. (And those weren’t worms, because they didn’t copy themselves and spread.)
paras.zh: 人工智能蠕虫的释放还有另一个实际障碍。与传统蠕虫相比，它们使用更多的计算能力并占用更多的空间。 Mirai 蠕虫病毒在 2016 年摧毁了包括 Reddit 和 Spotify 在内的一系列网站，其大小只有几千字节，而实验中的中型 AI 模型则有数十 GB。这仍然比 2026 年初成为头条新闻的“流氓人工智能”事件背后的大规模顶级模型要小得多。（这些不是蠕虫病毒，因为它们不会自我复制和传播。）

paras.en: Most devices — including typical laptop computers — don’t have enough space or the right kind of chips to run worm-capable AI models, Guan says. But new versions of devices, such as security cameras, are coming out with advanced hardware for running AI, researchers at the AI company Anthropic write. And at the same time, even smaller AI models are becoming more capable of sophisticated cyberattacks. These developments could expand the pool of devices an AI worm could exploit.
paras.zh: 关说，大多数设备——包括典型的笔记本电脑——没有足够的空间或合适的芯片来运行具有蠕虫能力的人工智能模型。但人工智能公司 Anthropic 的研究人员写道，新版本的设备（例如安全摄像头）正在推出，配备了运行人工智能的先进硬件。与此同时，更小的人工智能模型也变得更有能力进行复杂的网络攻击。这些发展可以扩大人工智能蠕虫可以利用的设备池。

paras.en: “The ingredients are converging” to make AI worms more realistic, Riegler says. How quickly they will converge is up for debate. Anthropic puts the timeline at months into the future, but both Riegler and Guan say it will probably take longer.
paras.zh: 里格勒说，“各种成分正在融合”，使人工智能蠕虫变得更加真实。他们会以多快的速度融合还有待讨论。 Anthropic 将时间表推迟了几个月，但里格勒和关都表示可能需要更长的时间。

paras.en: The Mirai worm spread itself through smart devices including home routers, security cameras and even baby monitors. It broke into these devices by trying a small set of common default usernames and passwords. “Just using this very simple technique, this Mirai botnet was able to infect hundreds of thousands of devices,” says cybersecurity expert Zane Ma of Oregon State University in Corvallis, who presented an analysis of the attack at a 2017 security symposium. High-profile downed sites such as Reddit were actually collateral damage: A small group of young hackers had created the worm to mess with gaming servers.
paras.zh: Mirai 蠕虫病毒通过家庭路由器、安全摄像头甚至婴儿监视器等智能设备进行传播。它通过尝试一小组常见的默认用户名和密码来侵入这些设备。 “仅使用这种非常简单的技术，这个 Mirai 僵尸网络就能够感染数十万台设备，”科瓦利斯俄勒冈州立大学的网络安全专家 Zane Ma 说道，他在 2017 年的安全研讨会上对此次攻击进行了分析。 Reddit 等备受瞩目的网站被关闭实际上是附带损害：一小群年轻的黑客创建了蠕虫病毒来扰乱游戏服务器。

paras.en: Rebooting an infected device cleared Mirai. Changing its default login credentials prevented reinfection through the same route. But an AI-powered worm might make cleaning up this type of cybersecurity breach much more difficult. Why? Because the AI worm acts more like an octopus, Guan says.
paras.zh: 重新启动受感染的设备可清除 Mirai。更改其默认登录凭据可防止通过同一途径再次感染。但人工智能驱动的蠕虫可能会使清理此类网络安全漏洞变得更加困难。为什么？关说，因为人工智能蠕虫的行为更像章鱼。

paras.en: Guan and colleagues tested this octopus-worm in a virtual network. Anchored by several powerful computers that each had a chip called a graphics processing unit, or GPU, the faux networks also contained simulations of smart devices, including office printers and security cameras.
paras.zh: 关和同事在虚拟网络中测试了这种章鱼蠕虫。这些人造网络以几台功能强大的计算机为基础，每台计算机都有一个称为图形处理单元（GPU）的芯片，还包含智能设备的模拟，包括办公室打印机和安全摄像头。

paras.en: The octopus’s AI model head started on a single machine with a GPU. From there it sent out tentacles to take control of smaller devices. Upon encountering a new device, the head would use AI to plan how its tentacle could hack in. Often, a hack wouldn’t work, but the octopus wouldn’t give up. It would use info about how it failed to come up with a new hack to try. That ability is “a new, hypercharged way of attacking systems,” Riegler says. Whenever it found a computer with a large enough GPU, it would copy its head onto that new machine.
paras.zh: 章鱼的人工智能模型头是在一台带有 GPU 的机器上启动的。它从那里伸出触手来控制较小的设备。当遇到新设备时，章鱼的头部会使用人工智能来计划其触手如何侵入。通常，侵入是行不通的，但章鱼不会放弃。它将使用有关它如何未能提出新的黑客尝试的信息。里格勒说，这种能力是“一种新的、强大的系统攻击方式”。每当它发现一台具有足够大 GPU 的计算机时，它就会将其头部复制到该新计算机上。

paras.en: An attacker would probably launch an octopus-style AI worm from the cloud. Click through this slideshow to see how it might spread autonomously. First, it takes over and copies itself onto a device with the right kind of hardware (chip icon) to house an AI model (first image). From there, it sends out tentacles (red arrows) to hack into any connected devices, like 3-D printers and security cameras (second image). Devices that don’t have enough space for the AI model become jumping-off points for the octopus-worm to discover new places to copy itself (third image).
paras.zh: 攻击者可能会从云端启动章鱼式人工智能蠕虫。点击这张幻灯片，看看它如何自动传播。首先，它接管并将自身复制到具有正确类型硬件（芯片图标）的设备上以容纳人工智能模型（第一张图片）。从那里，它会发出触手（红色箭头）来侵入任何连接的设备，例如 3D 打印机和安全摄像头（第二张图片）。没有足够空间容纳人工智能模型的设备成为章鱼蠕虫发现新位置来复制自身的起点（第三张图片）。

paras.en: The head could also search a simulated internet for information about newly discovered vulnerabilities. (The team didn’t connect it to the real internet for obvious reasons — protection against an AI octopus invasion — and spent considerable effort making sure their creation couldn’t escape the lab, Guan says.)
paras.zh: 该负责人还可以在模拟互联网上搜索有关新发现的漏洞的信息。 （关说，出于显而易见的原因，该团队没有将其连接到真正的互联网——防止人工智能章鱼入侵——并花了相当大的努力来确保他们的创造物无法逃出实验室。）

paras.en: The octopus-worm even came up with a way to survive a reboot, something Guan says they hadn’t asked it to do. The team posted a preprint of their findings at arXiv.org on June 2, and the paper is now going through peer review.
paras.zh: 章鱼蠕虫甚至想出了一种在重启后生存的方法，关说他们并没有要求它这样做。该团队于 6 月 2 日在 arXiv.org 上发布了他们的研究结果预印本，该论文目前正在接受同行评审。

paras.en: Meanwhile, at Anthropic, researchers showed another way an AI worm might work by building on Guan and his colleagues’ research. If an octopus-worm wasn’t weird enough, Anthropic dubbed its creation a “digital slime mold”, a name that captures the model’s slow, oozing behavior. Anthropic declined to comment for this story, but Guan says the company’s work shows that “unlike human reasoning, AI reasoning can be distributed.” That means an AI worm wouldn’t necessarily need to hijack a powerful computer to copy and run itself — it could spread its “thinking” out among smaller devices.
paras.zh: 与此同时，在 Anthropic，研究人员在关及其同事的研究基础上展示了人工智能蠕虫的另一种工作方式。如果章鱼蠕虫还不够奇怪的话，Anthropic 将其创造物称为“数字粘液霉菌”，这个名字反映了该模型缓慢、渗出的行为。 Anthropic 拒绝对此事发表评论，但关表示，该公司的工作表明“与人类推理不同，人工智能推理可以是分布式的”。这意味着人工智能蠕虫不一定需要劫持一台功能强大的计算机来复制和运行自己——它可以将其“思维”传播到较小的设备上。

paras.en: And that’s exactly what the slime mold version of an AI worm does. It breaks itself up and runs pieces of the model on multiple smaller devices. In their report posted online October 12, the Anthropic researchers used 15 Android smart TVs that they had networked together.
paras.zh: 这正是人工智能蠕虫的粘菌版本所做的事情。它会自行分解并在多个较小的设备上运行模型的各个部分。在 10 月 12 日在线发布的报告中，Anthropic 研究人员使用了 15 台联网的 Android 智能电视。

paras.en: Anthropic’s chopped-up model processes data thousands of times more slowly than what’s possible with GPUs similar to the ones Guan and colleagues relied on. That’s because the model’s data has to travel over internet connections that could take it all around the world during processing, rather than remaining in one place, within chips optimized for AI processing. That pace was too slow to demonstrate an ability to spread like a computer worm, Guan notes. So the Anthropic team ran a separate experiment with an AI worm running on GPUs that showed it could spread and adapt its attacks to different kinds of devices.
paras.zh: Anthropic 的分割模型处理数据的速度比关及其同事所依赖的 GPU 慢数千倍。这是因为该模型的数据必须通过互联网连接传输，在处理过程中可以将其传送到世界各地，而不是保留在针对人工智能处理优化的芯片内的一个地方。关指出，这种速度太慢，不足以证明其像计算机蠕虫一样传播的能力。因此，Anthropic 团队对在 GPU 上运行的 AI 蠕虫进行了一项单独的实验，结果表明它可以传播并使其攻击适应不同类型的设备。

paras.en: Whether AI worms are coming in months or whether we have longer to prepare, defenders should get ready now, Guan says. And AI worms do have weaknesses.
paras.zh: 关说，无论人工智能蠕虫会在几个月后出现，还是我们需要更长的时间来准备，防御者现在就应该做好准备。人工智能蠕虫确实有弱点。

paras.en: For one thing, the large size of an AI worm could be its downfall. Even if smaller AI models become more capable, these are still big programs that guzzle computing power. You might not notice if your fridge or microwave suddenly started sending lots of traffic onto the network, but your internet service provider would. They’d realize “there’s something weird going on on these devices,” Ma says. From there, they could quarantine affected devices, disconnecting them from the internet to prevent further spread.
paras.zh: 一方面，人工智能蠕虫的巨大尺寸可能是其失败的原因。即使较小的人工智能模型变得更加强大，这些仍然是消耗计算能力的大型程序。您可能不会注意到您的冰箱或微波炉是否突然开始向网络发送大量流量，但您的互联网服务提供商会注意到。马云说，他们会意识到“这些设备上发生了一些奇怪的事情”。从那里，他们可以隔离受影响的设备，断开它们与互联网的连接，以防止进一步传播。

paras.en: Ma also points out that most smart devices in a person’s home aren’t directly connected to the public internet. Most home networks use a router as a central hub, and that provides a layer of protection against a worm attack.
paras.zh: 马云还指出，家庭中的大多数智能设备都没有直接连接到公共互联网。大多数家庭网络使用路由器作为中央集线器，这提供了一层针对蠕虫攻击的保护。

paras.en: Strong passwords, regular updates and other normal security measures would also protect against the attacks demonstrated in both experiments, Riegler says.
paras.zh: 里格勒说，强密码、定期更新和其他正常的安全措施也可以防止这两个实验中展示的攻击。

paras.en: Guan and some colleagues are now testing specific defenses to stop AI worms, including devising an AI-driven defender. Trying to anticipate emerging threats and protect systems ahead of time is “what I’m passionate about,” Guan says. “We are working on the problem day and night.”
paras.zh: 关和一些同事现在正在测试阻止人工智能蠕虫的特定防御措施，包括设计人工智能驱动的防御程序。关说，尝试提前预测新出现的威胁并保护系统是“我热衷的事情”。 “我们正在夜以继日地解决这个问题。”

articles.title: Major Fossil Discovery in China Reveals New Secrets About Mysterious Hominin Ancestors
articles.author: Michael Irving

paras.en: Every family has some secrets – and the human family is no exception. Analysis of newly found fossils has revealed two surprises about our ancestor, Homo erectus.
paras.zh: 每个家庭都有一些秘密——人类家庭也不例外。对新发现的化石的分析揭示了关于我们的祖先直立人的两个令人惊讶的事情。

paras.en: It's the equivalent of discovering that grandpa had a secret vacation home in the tropics – and that he lived there for an extra 20 years after everyone thought he'd died.
paras.zh: 这相当于发现爷爷在热带地区有一处秘密度假屋，并且在所有人都认为他已经去世后，他又在那里住了 20 年。

paras.en: Homo erectus was one of the most successful hominins the world has ever known. The species was around for almost 2 million years, may have been the first to figure out how to use fire, and is thought to have been the first to leave Africa.
paras.zh: 直立人是世界上最成功的人类之一。该物种存在了近 200 万年，可能是第一个学会如何使用火的物种，并且被认为是第一个离开非洲的物种。

paras.en: H. erectus thrived in arid grasslands and savannas – open environments with sparse tree cover. And in the early Pleistocene, reduced global rainfall helped these habitats expand into new areas, and along with it went many of the animals that called these environments home.
paras.zh: 直立人在干旱的草原和稀树草原——树木稀疏的开放环境中繁衍生息。在更新世早期，全球降雨量减少帮助这些栖息地扩展到新的区域，许多以这些环境为家的动物也随之消失。

paras.en: That included H. erectus, which spread throughout Eurasia and Southeast Asia, following its favored habitat. It thrived in these areas for hundreds of thousands of years, giving rise to several descendant species.
paras.zh: 其中包括直立人，它沿着其喜爱的栖息地遍布欧亚大陆和东南亚。它在这些地区繁盛了数十万年，产生了几个后代物种。

paras.en: But as the environments changed again, H. erectus struggled to adapt to life in jungles and rainforests, paving the way for those descendant species – including little old Homo sapiens – to take over.
paras.zh: 但随着环境再次发生变化，直立人努力适应丛林和雨林的生活，为那些后代物种（包括小智人）的接管铺平了道路。

paras.en: Or at least, that's how scientists have long thought the story went. But two new papers published in the journal Nature could change the narrative.
paras.zh: 或者至少，科学家们长期以来一直认为故事是这样发生的。但《自然》杂志上发表的两篇新论文可能会改变这种说法。

paras.en: The findings come from a treasure trove of over 18,000 mammal fossils discovered in two caves, known as Baxian and Naxian, in southern China. Among the ancient remains of elephants, apes, pandas, tapirs, and rhinos, nine hominin teeth were recovered.
paras.zh: 这些发现来自于在中国南方的两个洞穴（称为八仙和纳仙）中发现的超过 18,000 块哺乳动物化石的宝库。在大象、猿、熊猫、貘和犀牛的古代遗骸中，发现了九颗古人类牙齿。

paras.en: In one study, an international team of scientists closely examined the teeth, and found that eight of them "show a combination of features usually found in H. erectus specimens".
paras.zh: 在一项研究中，一个国际科学家小组仔细检查了牙齿，发现其中八颗牙齿“显示出直立人标本中常见的特征组合”。

paras.en: Next, the team analyzed proteins in five of the teeth, and found that four of them had a protein pattern linked to Homo erectus.
paras.zh: 接下来，研究小组分析了五颗牙齿中的蛋白质，发现其中四颗牙齿具有与直立人相关的蛋白质模式。

paras.en: That said, there was one tiny change which led the researchers to conclude that "these specimens represent a previously unsampled H. erectus population."
paras.zh: 也就是说，有一个微小的变化导致研究人员得出结论：“这些标本代表了以前未采样的直立人种群。”

paras.en: One tooth, however, didn't quite fit the bill, with neither its physical features nor protein profile matching Homo erectus. It also didn't seem to be from a Neanderthal or modern human either.
paras.zh: 然而，其中一颗牙齿不太符合要求，它的物理特征和蛋白质特征都不符合直立人的特征。它似乎也不是来自尼安德特人或现代人类。

paras.en: There's a chance it's from a Denisovan – it doesn't match that protein sequence either, but there's only one reference genome available for that species, so it could just be that we don't have enough data, the team says.
paras.zh: 研究小组表示，它有可能来自丹尼索瓦人——它也不符合该蛋白质序列，但该物种只有一个参考基因组，因此可能只是我们没有足够的数据。

paras.en: Whatever it is, the strange tooth suggests that H. erectus wasn't the only hominin in the area at the time.
paras.zh: 不管是什么，这颗奇怪的牙齿表明直立人并不是当时该地区唯一的古人类。

paras.en: Speaking of time, one of the most surprising finds was that these teeth are far younger than expected. Radiometric dating of the fossils and the sediments they were buried in indicated they were between 184,000 and 324,000 years old.
paras.zh: 说到时间，最令人惊讶的发现之一是这些牙齿比预期的要年轻得多。对化石及其埋藏沉积物进行的放射性测年表明，它们的年龄在 184,000 至 324,000 年间。

paras.en: The fossil record for H. erectus in China is pretty rich and detailed for more than a million years – but it almost completely dries up around 400,000 years ago. The new specimens indicate the hominin survived in the area for much longer than previously thought.
paras.zh: 中国直立人的化石记录相当丰富且详细，可追溯至超过一百万年，但在大约 40 万年前几乎完全枯竭。新的标本表明，古人类在该地区生存的时间比之前想象的要长得多。

paras.en: The second study dug into how Homo erectus might have hung on for those extra millennia. By that time, the environment had shifted from its preferred grassland home to thick, tropical rainforests – a habitat thought homely only to Homo sapiens.
paras.zh: 第二项研究深入探讨了直立人是如何存活了数千年的。到那时，环境已经从它最喜欢的草原转移到了茂密的热带雨林——一个被认为只有智人才适宜居住的栖息地。

paras.en: The team analyzed the isotopes and trace elements of some of the teeth to find out where their owners had hailed from, and what kinds of foods they'd eaten in life.
paras.zh: 研究小组分析了一些牙齿的同位素和微量元素，以了解它们的主人来自哪里，以及它们生前吃过哪些食物。

paras.en: Sure enough, the carbon in their teeth came mostly from the vegetation of tropical forests with a dense, closed canopy. That's consistent with other fossil evidence showing that was the dominant environment in that place and time.
paras.zh: 果然，它们牙齿中的碳主要来自树冠茂密、封闭的热带森林的植被。这与其他化石证据一致，表明那是那个地点和时间的主导环境。

paras.en: "This demonstrates that H. erectus was, at minimum, capable of persisting among rainforest fauna, even if such habitats did not represent its optimal ecological niche," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“这表明直立人至少能够在雨林动物群中生存，即使这些栖息地并不代表其最佳生态位。”

paras.en: Analysis of the strontium isotopes in the teeth revealed that this less-than-ideal environment didn't ruin their travel plans.
paras.zh: 对牙齿中锶同位素的分析表明，这种不太理想的环境并没有破坏他们的旅行计划。

paras.en: They seemed to have migrated at times, possibly traveling as far away as what is now northern Vietnam – some 250 kilometers (155 miles) away from the caves where their remains were found.
paras.zh: 它们似乎有时会迁徙，可能远至现在的越南北部——距发现其遗骸的洞穴约 250 公里（155 英里）。

paras.en: The bottom line is that there's always more to learn about our own family history – and we shouldn't underestimate our ancestors.
paras.zh: 最重要的是，关于我们自己的家族历史，我们总是有更多的东西需要了解——我们不应该低估我们的祖先。

paras.en: "Rather than being restricted to open savanna or woodland habitats, as traditionally assumed, these populations persisted in closed-canopy tropical rainforests while simultaneously engaging in potential long-distance mobility across diverse ecological and geological landscapes," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“这些种群并不像传统上认为的那样仅限于开放的稀树草原或林地栖息地，而是持续存在于封闭的热带雨林中，同时在不同的生态和地质景观中进行潜在的长距离流动。”

articles.title: Scientists Developed 'Smart Floss' That Uses Gunk Between Your Teeth to Track Metabolism
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: The health of our teeth and gums is closely connected to the health of our bodies and brains.
paras.zh: 我们的牙齿和牙龈的健康与我们的身体和大脑的健康密切相关。

paras.en: In recent years, growing evidence has begun to show that poor oral health is associated with a slew of other concerning conditions, including dementia, diabetes, stroke, heart disease, cancer, and even death.
paras.zh: 近年来，越来越多的证据开始表明，口腔健康状况不佳与许多其他令人担忧的疾病有关，包括痴呆、糖尿病、中风、心脏病、癌症，甚至死亡。

paras.en: A new flossing device that captures the gunk between our teeth could be a high-tech way to monitor oral health and the body's metabolism at the same time – all from the comfort of your home.
paras.zh: 一种新的牙线装置可以捕捉牙齿之间的粘稠物，它可能是一种同时监测口腔健康和身体新陈代谢的高科技方法——这一切都可以在舒适的家中进行。

paras.en: In a recent 'test run' among small groups of people, published in Science Advances, the tool's glucose and uric acid readings closely tracked those from a blood test.
paras.zh: 最近发表在《科学进展》上的一项针对小群体的“测试”显示，该工具的血糖和尿酸读数与血液测试的读数密切相关。

paras.en: It could also use acidity and hydrogen peroxide measurements to reliably estimate the size of a person's gum pockets, an indicator dentists often use when diagnosing periodontal (gum) disease.
paras.zh: 它还可以使用酸度和过氧化氢测量来可靠地估计一个人牙龈袋的大小，这是牙医在诊断牙周（牙龈）疾病时经常使用的指标。

paras.en: The device was invented by a team led by biotechnologist Hnin Yin Yin Nyein at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST), and they argue it has capabilities that have eluded the field for decades.
paras.zh: 该设备是由香港科技大学（HKUST）生物技术专家 Hnin Yin Yin Nyein 领导的团队发明的，他们认为该设备具有数十年来该领域一直未能实现的功能。

paras.en: The unique contraption is shaped like a typical dental flosser with a complex pulley system that harvests fluid and directs it into a dedicated microfluidic chamber with biosensors.
paras.zh: 这种独特的装置的形状像典型的牙线器，具有复杂的滑轮系统，可以收集液体并将其引导到带有生物传感器的专用微流体室中。

paras.en: Within minutes of flossing, these sensors can measure uric acid, glucose, hydrogen peroxide, and pH in the fluid.
paras.zh: 使用牙线后几分钟内，这些传感器就可以测量液体中的尿酸、葡萄糖、过氧化氢和 pH 值。

paras.en: The results are then sent wirelessly to a smartphone.
paras.zh: 然后结果被无线发送到智能手机。

paras.en: The fluid that the device is capturing is distinct from saliva. It's called gingival crevicular fluid (GCF), and it exists in the grooves around and between teeth.
paras.zh: 该设备捕获的液体与唾液不同。它被称为龈沟液（GCF），存在于牙齿周围和牙齿之间的凹槽中。

paras.en: Because the GCF sits close to the surface of the gums, it exchanges metabolites, proteins, and inflammatory markers with the bloodstream.
paras.zh: 由于 GCF 靠近牙龈表面，因此它与血液交换代谢物、蛋白质和炎症标记物。

paras.en: For decades now, scientists have tried to use this fluid to analyze gum disease, and other health conditions, but it is produced in very small amounts that are hard to capture.
paras.zh: 几十年来，科学家们一直试图使用这种液体来分析牙龈疾病和其他健康状况，但它的产生量非常小，很难捕获。

paras.en: When a person flosses, however, it uproots some of the GCF.
paras.zh: 然而，当一个人使用牙线时，它会连根拔起一些GCF。

paras.en: That's why scientists in China decided to use a flossing system to harvest this precious liquid.
paras.zh: 这就是为什么中国的科学家决定使用牙线系统来收集这种珍贵的液体。

paras.en: Their device was tested in preliminary trials, not only on healthy participants, but also on those with diabetes, high uric acid levels (known as hyperuricemia), and poor oral health.
paras.zh: 他们的设备在初步试验中进行了测试，不仅针对健康参与者，还针对患有糖尿病、高尿酸水平（称为高尿酸血症）和口腔健康状况不佳的患者。

paras.en: The readouts were distinct for each ailment.
paras.zh: 每种疾病的读数都是不同的。

paras.en: Glucose levels in flossing fluid, for instance, closely matched measurements in the bloodstream.
paras.zh: 例如，牙线液中的葡萄糖水平与血液中的测量值非常匹配。

paras.en: What's more, uric acid levels were strongly correlated with blood levels.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，尿酸水平与血液水平密切相关。

paras.en: The findings suggest that invasive blood tests that track glucose and uric acid levels could potentially be rivaled by a non-invasive flossing system
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，追踪血糖和尿酸水平的侵入性血液测试可能会被非侵入性牙线系统所竞争

paras.en: "No home monitoring tool simultaneously addresses systemic metabolism and oral inflammation – a critical gap for patients with diabetes, hyperuricemia, and periodontitis, where metabolic dysregulation worsens gum disease and oral inflammation impairs metabolic control," write the authors of the study.
paras.zh: 该研究的作者写道：“没有一种家庭监测工具能够同时解决全身代谢和口腔炎症问题，这对于糖尿病、高尿酸血症和牙周炎患者来说是一个关键差距，因为代谢失调会加剧牙龈疾病，而口腔炎症会损害代谢控制。”

paras.en: An invention like this could help fill that gap, but it still requires some tweaking and testing.
paras.zh: 像这样的发明可以帮助填补这一空白，但它仍然需要一些调整和测试。

paras.en: For instance, saliva made up nearly half of the fluid collected along with GCF, and blood can also get mixed in.
paras.zh: 例如，唾液占与 GCF 一起收集的液体的近一半，并且血液也可能混入其中。

paras.en: When researchers tested saliva on its own, it did not seem to harbor much information on glucose levels at all. But it's possible that blood-contaminated samples do.
paras.zh: 当研究人员单独测试唾液时，它似乎根本没有包含太多关于葡萄糖水平的信息。但血液污染的样本也有可能会出现这种情况。

paras.en: "Despite these limitations, the system is designed with clinical translation in mind," argues the team.
paras.zh: “尽管存在这些限制，该系统的设计还是考虑到了临床翻译，”该团队认为。

paras.en: They have called for a future clinical trial to see whether GCF-guided monitoring improves clinical outcomes in patients with both diabetes and gum disease.
paras.zh: 他们呼吁未来进行一项临床试验，看看 GCF 引导的监测是否可以改善糖尿病和牙龈疾病患者的临床结果。

paras.en: "By converting a daily habit practiced by billions into a diagnostic act, this work establishes native GCF as an accessible biofluid for noninvasive, personalized health care," the authors conclude.
paras.zh: 作者总结道：“通过将数十亿人的日常习惯转化为诊断行为，这项工作将天然 GCF 确立为一种可用于无创、个性化医疗保健的生物流体。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Science Advances.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学进展》上。

articles.title: For The First Time, 4 Radiation Belts Appeared Around Earth in 2024
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: Many of the most consequential happenings in the Universe are generally invisible to our human eyes (oh, to be a spacefaring mantis shrimp!).
paras.zh: 宇宙中许多最重要的事件通常是我们人眼看不见的（哦，作为一只太空螳螂虾！）。

paras.en: Even our near-Earth environment is awash in unseen phenomena. Our planet is surrounded by two immense cosmic doughnuts of radiation known as the Van Allen Belts, discovered at the dawn of the space age in 1958 by the first US satellite, Explorer 1, and named after physicist James Van Allen.
paras.zh: 甚至我们的近地环境也充满了看不见的现象。我们的星球被两个巨大的宇宙辐射甜甜圈包围，称为范艾伦带，是 1958 年太空时代初期由美国第一颗卫星“探索者 1”号发现的，并以物理学家詹姆斯·范艾伦的名字命名。

paras.en: These two toroidal structures comprise an inner belt, predominantly full of higher-energy protons, and an outer belt, mostly full of high-energy electrons, situated beyond low-Earth orbit.
paras.zh: 这两个环形结构包括一个主要充满高能质子的内带和一个主要充满高能电子的外带，位于近地轨道之外。

paras.en: These particles originate from intense solar storms and cosmic rays, the latter produced by massive dying stars, and are then trapped in an orbital zoo around our thankfully magnetic Earth.
paras.zh: 这些粒子源自强烈的太阳风暴和宇宙射线，后者是由巨大的垂死恒星产生的，然后被困在我们幸运的磁性地球周围的轨道动物园中。

paras.en: Normally, only these two (inner and outer) belts are present.
paras.zh: 通常，仅存在这两个（内和外）带。

paras.en: But for the first time, astronomers observed four distinct electron belts following the exceptionally energetic geomagnetic storm that accosted our planet on 11 May 2024 – creating a short-lived, multi-headed Hydra of radiation.
paras.zh: 但在 2024 年 5 月 11 日异常活跃的地磁风暴席卷地球之后，天文学家首次观察到了四个不同的电子带，形成了短暂的多头九头蛇辐射。

paras.en: As described in a recent study published in the journal npj Space Exploration, the researchers explored this ephemerally unique occurrence using the Energetic Particle Telescope (EPT) instrument aboard ESA's PROBA-V satellite, which occupies a Sun-synchronous polar orbit at an altitude of 820 kilometers (more than 500 miles) above our home planet.
paras.zh: 正如最近发表在《npj Space Exploration》杂志上的一项研究所述，研究人员利用欧空局 PROBA-V 卫星上的高能粒子望远镜 (EPT) 仪器探索了这一短暂的独特现象，该卫星占据了太阳同步极轨道，高度为我们地球上方 820 公里（超过 500 英里）。

paras.en: This exceptional occurrence, called the "Mother's Day event", was the strongest geomagnetic storm in 20 years.
paras.zh: 这一特殊事件被称为“母亲节事件”，是 20 年来最强的地磁风暴。

paras.en: And although it supplied a massive influx of electrons into our near-Earth environs, the four-electron-belt configuration appeared a bit later due to the local depletion, rather than addition, of electrons.
paras.zh: 尽管它向我们的近地环境提供了大量的电子流入，但由于电子的局部耗尽而不是添加，四电子带配置出现得稍晚一些。

paras.en: As electromagnetic interactions swept the electrons from the belts, they created temporary new slot regions, separating the belts into four distinct entities.
paras.zh: 当电磁相互作用从带上扫过电子时，它们产生了临时的新槽区域，将带分成四个不同的实体。

paras.en: This process progressed several days to weeks after the storm, creating three electron belts and then the never-before-observed four-electron-belt configuration by June 2024. Then, by August 2024, the normal two-belt formation had recovered.
paras.zh: 这一过程在风暴发生后几天到几周内进行，形成了三个电子带，然后到 2024 年 6 月形成了以前从未观察到的四电子带结构。然后，到 2024 年 8 月，正常的两电子带结构已经恢复。

paras.en: We've seen a three-belt system in 2012, and then multiple times between 2024 and 2026 after sizable geomagnetic storms, including in October 2024, a few days after the second-strongest such storm of the past 20 years.
paras.zh: 我们在 2012 年看到了三带系统，然后在 2024 年至 2026 年发生大规模地磁风暴后多次出现，包括 2024 年 10 月，即过去 20 年来第二强的此类风暴发生几天后。

paras.en: "It is surprising to find four belts and so often three belts recently, while only two belts were observed before. This means that new mechanisms of loss or trapping appeared recently," first author Viviane Pierrard, head of the solar wind division and senior research scientist at the Royal Belgian Institute for Space Aeronomy, tells ScienceAlert via email.
paras.zh: “令人惊讶的是，最近发现了四个带，甚至经常发现了三个带，而之前只观察到了两个带。这意味着最近出现了新的损失或捕获机制，”第一作者、比利时皇家太空航空研究所太阳风部门负责人兼高级研究科学家 Viviane Pierrard 通过电子邮件告诉 ScienceAlert。

paras.en: Interestingly, astronomers did not observe the three-belt configuration during the peak of the Sun's activity, or solar maximum, in Solar Cycle 24, the previous 11-year solar cycle which ended in December 2019. During this maximum, the solar flux was injected directly into the inner belt.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，天文学家在第 24 太阳周期（于 2019 年 12 月结束的上一个 11 年太阳周期）太阳活动高峰期或太阳极大期期间没有观察到三带结构。在此极大期期间，太阳通量直接注入内带。

paras.en: Instead of orally ingesting a 12-pack of Krispy Kremes and letting it settle metabolically, imagine having them reverse-liposuctioned straight into one's thighs.
paras.zh: 与其口服 12 包 Krispy Kremes 并让它通过新陈代谢解决，不如想象一下将它们直接反向抽脂到大腿上。

paras.en: "The multiple Van Allen belts clearly appear due to the arrival of coronal mass ejections disturbing the space environment of the Earth and increasing the flux in the radiation belts," the researchers summarize.
paras.zh: 研究人员总结道：“由于日冕物质抛射的到来扰乱了地球的空间环境并增加了辐射带的通量，因此多个范艾伦带的出现明显地出现了。”

paras.en: In other words, solar outbursts of varying intensities create magnetic field disturbances, which drive electrons to different 'depths' into the normally two-belt structure around Earth.
paras.zh: 换句话说，不同强度的太阳爆发会产生磁场扰动，从而将电子驱动到不同的“深度”，进入地球周围通常为两带的结构。

paras.en: Sometimes these electrons are deposited directly into one of the existing belts, but else-wise they may be trapped between them.
paras.zh: 有时这些电子会直接沉积到现有的带之一中，但否则它们可能会被困在它们之间。

paras.en: They thus interact with numerous types of electromagnetic waves, which can scatter the electrons into our atmosphere and create slots between the electron belts, separating them into multiple parts.
paras.zh: 因此，它们与多种类型的电磁波相互作用，电磁波可以将电子散射到我们的大气中，并在电子带之间形成缝隙，将它们分成多个部分。

paras.en: These electromagnetic influences then cause the trapped electrons in the new belts to gradually drift inward or outward across Earth's magnetic field lines (or "shells") over the course of a month or so, and the normal two-belt configuration returns, until the next geomagnetic storm.
paras.zh: 然后，这些电磁影响导致新带中被捕获的电子在一个月左右的时间内逐渐向内或向外漂移穿过地球磁场线（或“壳”），并且正常的两带配置返回，直到下一次地磁风暴。

paras.en: Of course, this is an incredibly complex process depending on the aforementioned factors, atmospheric gas atoms and plasma, as well as lightning discharges and even human activities like electromagnetic emitters used for submarine communications.
paras.zh: 当然，这是一个极其复杂的过程，取决于上述因素、大气气体原子和等离子体，以及闪电放电，甚至人类活动，例如用于海底通信的电磁发射器。

paras.en: The "electrons and protons are dangerous for spacecraft, mainly for electronic devices and solar cells, and astronauts, [increasing risks of issues like cancers and cataracts] due to their very high energy," Pierrard explained over email.
paras.zh: 皮拉德在电子邮件中解释说：“电子和质子对航天器（主要是电子设备和太阳能电池）以及宇航员来说是危险的，[增加癌症和白内障等问题的风险]，因为它们的能量非常高。”

paras.en: In fact, even a single hit from such a particle can disrupt our ever-more sensitive instruments.
paras.zh: 事实上，即使是这样的粒子的一次撞击也会破坏我们越来越敏感的仪器。

paras.en: Therefore, the scientists involved in this study hope to further study this intricate interplay of solar and geomagnetic forces, especially as humanity increases its cosmic footprint.
paras.zh: 因此，参与这项研究的科学家希望进一步研究太阳力和地磁力之间复杂的相互作用，特别是在人类扩大其宇宙足迹的情况下。

paras.en: "Understanding how these long-lived additional belts form and evolve provides new insight into the processes that trap and remove energetic particles in Earth's magnetic field," the researchers conclude.
paras.zh: 研究人员总结道：“了解这些长寿的额外带是如何形成和演化的，为了解地球磁场中捕获和消除高能粒子的过程提供了新的见解。”

paras.en: The research has been published in npj Space Exploration.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在 npj Space Exploration 上。

articles.title: Bizarre deep-sea fish with a see-through head captured in stunning 4K

paras.en: Bizarre deep-sea fish with a see-through head captured in stunning 4K
paras.zh: 令人惊叹的 4K 图像捕捉到头部透明的奇异深海鱼

paras.en: - Deep-sea researchers have captured stunning new footage of an extraordinarily rare fish with a transparent head and rotating eyes nearly 2,000 feet beneath the ocean's surface. Known as the barreleye fish, this bizarre creature uses its upward-pointing eyes to spot prey before rotating them forward to track its next meal, all while a transparent dome protects them.
paras.zh: - 深海研究人员在海面以下近 2,000 英尺处拍摄到了一种极其罕见的鱼类的惊人新镜头，该鱼具有透明的头部和旋转的眼睛。这种奇特的生物被称为桶眼鱼，它用向上的眼睛来发现猎物，然后将它们向前旋转以追踪下一顿饭，同时透明的圆顶保护它们。

paras.en: A rare encounter nearly 2,000 feet beneath the ocean's surface gave scientists an extraordinary opportunity to film one of the deep sea's most unusual creatures. Researchers from the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute (MBARI) spotted a barreleye fish (Macropinna microstoma), a mysterious species known for its transparent head and remarkable eyes that can rotate to track prey.
paras.zh: 在海面以下近 2,000 英尺处的一次罕见遭遇，为科学家们提供了一个绝佳的机会来拍摄深海最不寻常的生物之一。蒙特利湾水族馆研究所 (MBARI) 的研究人员发现了一种桶眼鱼（Macropinna microstoma），这是一种神秘的物种，以其透明的头部和可以旋转追踪猎物的非凡眼睛而闻名。

paras.en: The discovery occurred during an expedition aboard the research vessel David Packard. It marked only the eleventh time MBARI scientists have encountered this elusive fish during nearly four decades of ocean exploration.
paras.zh: 这一发现是在大卫·帕卡德号研究船的一次探险期间发现的。这标志着 MBARI 科学家在近四十年的海洋探索中第十一次遇到这种难以捉摸的鱼类。

paras.en: Members of MBARI's Biodiversity and Biooptics Team were investigating marine life approximately 90 kilometers (55 miles) offshore when they spotted the fish about 600 meters (1,970 feet) below the surface. Using the remotely operated vehicle (ROV) Doc Ricketts, the researchers were filming and collecting deep-sea organisms when the unexpected visitor appeared.
paras.zh: MBARI 生物多样性和生物光学团队的成员在近海约 90 公里（55 英里）处调查海洋生物时，在海面以下约 600 米（1,970 英尺）处发现了这条鱼。当研究人员使用遥控潜水器（ROV）Doc Ricketts 拍摄和收集深海生物时，意外的访客出现了。

paras.en: "Seeing a barreleye fish is a rare treat. Crew from across the ship joined the science team in the control room, mesmerized by this remarkable animal. Deep-sea animals capture the imagination, creating wonder and awe that we hope will inspire stewardship of the largest living space on Earth," said Senior Scientist Steven Haddock.
paras.zh: “看到桶眼鱼是一种难得的享受。来自船上的船员们加入了控制室的科学团队，被这种非凡的动物迷住了。深海动物激发了人们的想象力，创造了奇迹和敬畏，我们希望这将激发对地球上最大的生存空间的管理，”高级科学家史蒂文·哈多克说。

paras.en: A Surprise Encounter Deep in the Pacific Ocean
paras.zh: 太平洋深处的惊喜邂逅

paras.en: The discovery was an unexpected highlight of the eight-day Diving Deep for Delicate Drifters expedition. Haddock and his colleagues had primarily been investigating gelatinous marine animals, including jellyfish, siphonophores, and ctenophores, also known as comb jellies. Their research seeks to understand how these delicate organisms have evolved to survive in the open ocean at great depths.
paras.zh: 这一发现是为期八天的“Diving Deep for Delicate Drifters”探险之旅的一个意想不到的亮点。哈多克和他的同事主要研究凝胶状海洋动物，包括水母、管水母和栉水母（也称为栉水母）。他们的研究旨在了解这些脆弱的生物体如何进化以在深海中生存。

paras.en: To investigate life throughout the water column, the team combined blue-water scuba dives near the surface with remotely operated vehicle surveys hundreds of meters below. These complementary approaches allowed researchers to observe and collect animals living in very different parts of the ocean.
paras.zh: 为了调查整个水体的生命，该团队将近海面的蓝水水肺潜水与数百米以下的遥控车辆调查结合起来。这些互补的方法使研究人员能够观察和收集生活在海洋不同地区的动物。

paras.en: The barreleye appeared just as the day's underwater operations were coming to an end. The ROV pilots were "flying" Doc Ricketts toward the surface for recovery when Research Specialist Shannon Johnson noticed the unusual fish and immediately asked them to stop.
paras.zh: 就在当天的水下作业即将结束时，桶眼鱼出现了。当研究专家香农·约翰逊注意到这条不寻常的鱼并立即要求他们停下来时，ROV 飞行员正在将里基茨博士“驾驶”到水面进行回收。

paras.en: Most of the scientists had already moved to the ship's wet lab, where they were preparing to catalog specimens collected during the dive. When word spread about the sighting, they hurried back to the control room, accompanied by crew members eager to see the extraordinary animal. The rare encounter provided an exciting conclusion to a busy and productive week of exploration.
paras.zh: 大多数科学家已经转移到船上的湿实验室，他们正准备对潜水期间收集的标本进行编目。当目击事件的消息传开后，他们在渴望看到这只非凡动物的船员的陪同下匆忙返回控制室。这次罕见的邂逅为忙碌而富有成效的一周探索提供了令人兴奋的结论。

paras.en: How the Barreleye Fish Uses Its Transparent Head to Hunt
paras.zh: 桶眼鱼如何利用透明的头部捕猎

paras.en: The barreleye's strange appearance is more than a biological curiosity. Its unusual anatomy helps it find food in the ocean's twilight zone, a dimly lit region where sunlight is faint and spotting prey can be difficult.
paras.zh: 桶眼鱼的奇怪外观不仅仅是一种生物学上的好奇心。它不同寻常的解剖结构有助于它在海洋的暮光区寻找食物，这是一个光线昏暗的区域，阳光微弱，很难发现猎物。

paras.en: Earlier observations by MBARI Senior Scientist Bruce Robison and Research Specialist Kim Reisenbichler helped scientists understand how this remarkable fish hunts.
paras.zh: MBARI 高级科学家 Bruce Robison 和研究专家 Kim Reisenbichler 的早期观察帮助科学家了解了这种非凡鱼类的捕食方式。

paras.en: Rather than constantly swimming in search of food, Macropinna can remain nearly motionless in the water, supported by its large fins, which provide both stability and precise control over its movements. Its tubular eyes normally point upward, allowing it to watch for the faint silhouettes of animals passing overhead.
paras.zh: Macropinna 不会不断地游泳寻找食物，而是可以在水中保持几乎一动不动，由其大鳍支撑，这既提供了稳定性，又提供了对其运动的精确控制。它的管状眼睛通常指向上方，使其能够观察头顶上掠过的动物的微弱轮廓。

paras.en: Once the fish detects something worth eating, its eyes can rotate within a transparent dome of tissue covering the top of its head. This unusual ability allows the barreleye to maintain visual contact with prey as it changes position to capture it.
paras.zh: 一旦鱼发现有值得吃的东西，它的眼睛就会在覆盖其头顶的透明组织圆顶内旋转。这种不寻常的能力使得桶眼鱼在改变位置捕捉猎物时能够与猎物保持视觉接触。

paras.en: The clear, gelatinous covering serves another important purpose. Barreleyes can feed on small crustaceans trapped among the stinging tentacles of deep-sea siphonophores, which are colonial animals related to jellyfish. The protective dome helps shield the fish's sensitive eyes while it retrieves its meal.
paras.zh: 透明的凝胶状覆盖物还有另一个重要用途。桶眼鱼可以捕食深海管水母带刺触须中的小型甲壳类动物，管水母是与水母有亲缘关系的群居动物。保护性圆顶有助于保护鱼在取餐时敏感的眼睛。

paras.en: Rare 4K Footage Reveals Extraordinary Details
paras.zh: 罕见的 4K 镜头揭示非凡细节

paras.en: Scientists were able to spend approximately 20 minutes watching the barreleye during the encounter. Using the high-resolution 4K camera aboard Doc Ricketts, they recorded unusually detailed views of its anatomy and movements.
paras.zh: 在这次遭遇中，科学家们花了大约 20 分钟的时间观察桶眼鱼。他们使用 Doc Ricketts 上的高分辨率 4K 摄像机记录了其解剖结构和运动的异常详细的视图。

paras.en: The team also adjusted the vehicle's lighting to make the fish's transparent head shield easier to observe. These changes helped reveal the unusual structures that make this species so distinctive.
paras.zh: 研究小组还调整了车辆的照明，使鱼的透明头罩更容易观察。这些变化有助于揭示使该物种如此独特的不寻常结构。

paras.en: ROV Pilot/Technician Cameron Law brought Doc Ricketts close enough to capture additional footage with the vehicle's virtual reality camera. The resulting 3D stereo imagery provides another perspective on the fish and could eventually be used in educational programs and public outreach.
paras.zh: ROV 飞行员/技术员 Cameron Law 将 Doc Ricketts 带到足够近的位置，以便使用车辆的虚拟现实相机捕捉更多镜头。由此产生的 3D 立体图像提供了了解鱼类的另一个视角，最终可用于教育项目和公共宣传。

paras.en: "Macropinna reminds us of the surprising ways that animals have adapted to thrive in the ocean's midwater," said Haddock. "So many of them survive by looking for subtle optical cues, like a shadow passing overhead, and this sets off evolutionary competition, pitting bioluminescent camouflage against increasingly sophisticated visual capabilities."
paras.zh: “Macropinna 让我们想起动物如何适应在海洋中层水域繁衍生息，”哈多克说。 “它们中的许多人通过寻找微妙的光学线索来生存，比如头顶掠过的影子，这引发了进化竞争，使生物发光伪装与日益复杂的视觉能力形成对立。”

paras.en: An Extraordinary Sighting After Nearly 7,000 Deep-Sea Dives
paras.zh: 近 7,000 次深海潜水后的非凡目击

paras.en: The rarity of the encounter becomes even more striking when considering MBARI's extensive exploration history. Over nearly 40 years, the institute has conducted approximately 7,000 remotely operated vehicle dives and accumulated more than 41,000 hours of deep-sea video. Despite that enormous effort, researchers have recorded just 11 encounters with Macropinna microstoma.
paras.zh: 考虑到 MBARI 广泛的探索历史，这次遭遇的罕见性就变得更加惊人。近40年来，该研究所已进行约7,000次遥控潜水器潜水，积累了超过41,000小时的深海视频。尽管付出了巨大的努力，研究人员仅记录了 11 次与巨羽小口虫的遭遇。

paras.en: MBARI's previous sighting of Macropinna occurred in 2021. The latest encounter represents two important firsts for the institute: its first 4K footage of this species and its first observation of the fish from the new flagship research vessel David Packard.
paras.zh: MBARI 上一次目击 Macropinna 发生在 2021 年。最近的一次遭遇代表了该研究所的两个重要的第一：首次拍摄该物种的 4K 镜头，以及在新旗舰研究船 David Packard 上首次观察到这种鱼。

paras.en: MBARI scientists have also encountered other members of the barreleye family during their ocean expeditions. This summer, researchers working with Schmidt Ocean Institute in the mid-Atlantic Ocean recorded another unusual deep-sea species, the binocular fish (Winteria telescopa).
paras.zh: MBARI 的科学家在海洋探险期间还遇到了桶眼鱼家族的其他成员。今年夏天，与大西洋中部施密特海洋研究所合作的研究人员记录了另一种不寻常的深海物种，即双目鱼（Winteria telescopa）。

paras.en: Together, these encounters provide rare opportunities to observe the remarkable adaptations that allow animals to survive far beneath the ocean's surface, where light is scarce and much of the marine environment remains unexplored.
paras.zh: 总之，这些遭遇提供了难得的机会来观察动物的非凡适应能力，这些适应能力使动物能够在远离海洋表面的地方生存，那里光线稀缺，大部分海洋环境仍未被探索。

paras.en: The Diving Deep for Delicate Drifters expedition was supported through the David and Lucile Packard Foundation's longstanding commitment to MBARI's scientific research.
paras.zh: “Diving Deep for Delicate Drifters”探险活动得到了 David and Lucile Packard 基金会对 MBARI 科学研究的长期承诺的支持。

articles.title: More than a billion years of Earth's history vanished. Scientists may finally know why

paras.en: More than a billion years of Earth's history vanished. Scientists may finally know why
paras.zh: 超过十亿年的地球历史消失了。科学家可能终于知道原因了

paras.en: - Scientists may have finally explained why up to more than a billion years of Earth's geological history are missing from rocks around the world. New research suggests that powerful currents deep inside the planet slowly raised and lowered entire continents, allowing erosion to erase vast stretches of geological history before they were buried and preserved.
paras.zh: - 科学家们可能终于解释了为什么世界各地的岩石中缺失了长达十亿多年的地球地质历史。新的研究表明，地球深处的强大水流缓慢地抬升和降低了整个大陆，从而使侵蚀作用消除了大片地质历史，然后才将其埋葬和保存下来。

paras.en: More than a billion years of Earth's geological history are missing from some of the planet's rock formations. Scientists have debated the cause of this enormous gap for decades, but new research suggests that the answer may lie in the slow movement of entire continents, driven by powerful forces deep inside Earth.
paras.zh: 地球的一些岩层缺失了超过十亿年的地球地质历史。几十年来，科学家们一直在争论这一巨大差距的原因，但新的研究表明，答案可能在于整个大陆在地球深处强大力量的驱动下缓慢移动。

paras.en: A study led by a PhD candidate at the University of Wollongong (UOW) offers a new explanation for the Great Unconformity, one of geology's most enduring mysteries. Published in the journal Nature, the findings suggest that ancient continents gradually rose and sank over hundreds of millions of years as hot rock moved through Earth's interior. These changes in elevation may have allowed erosion to remove enormous amounts of rock, erasing vast stretches of the planet's geological record.
paras.zh: 卧龙岗大学 (UOW) 的一名博士生领导的一项研究为地质学最持久的谜团之一——大不整合面提供了新的解释。发表在《自然》杂志上的研究结果表明，随着热岩石穿过地球内部，古代大陆在数亿年的时间里逐渐上升和下沉。这些海拔变化可能导致侵蚀去除了大量的岩石，从而抹去了地球上大片的地质记录。

paras.en: Lead author Santosh Dhungana, a UOW PhD candidate, explained that although researchers have proposed numerous explanations for the Great Unconformity, few have been rigorously tested against the long-term behavior of Earth's interior.
paras.zh: 主要作者、伍伦贡大学博士生桑托什·杜加纳 (Santosh Dhungana) 解释说，尽管研究人员对大不整合提出了多种解释，但很少有经过严格的地球内部长期行为测试。

paras.en: "Imagine a book where a huge section in the middle has been ripped out. The Great Unconformity is that gap in Earth's story, with the narrative jumping from the early chapters straight to a much later part of the story. Our research suggests these pages weren't lost by chance," he said.
paras.zh: “想象一下，一本书的中间很大一部分被撕掉了。大不整合是地球故事中的一个空白，叙述从早期章节直接跳到故事的后期部分。我们的研究表明这些页面并不是偶然丢失的，”他说。

paras.en: Earth's Mysterious Missing Billion Years
paras.zh: 地球神秘消失了数十亿年

paras.en: Normally, layers of sedimentary rock accumulate over time, creating a geological timeline in which older rocks lie beneath younger ones. Scientists can study these layers to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years.
paras.zh: 通常，沉积岩层会随着时间的推移而积累，形成一条地质时间线，其中较古老的岩石位于较年轻的岩石之下。科学家可以研究这些层来重建古代环境并了解地球在数十亿年来如何变化。

paras.en: Yet this timeline contains a remarkable interruption. At numerous locations worldwide, sedimentary rocks dating to the Cambrian period, around 540 million years ago, rest directly on much older crystalline rocks, including granite that can be more than a billion years old. The intervening geological layers are absent, leaving an enormous break in the record known as the Great Unconformity.
paras.zh: 然而，这个时间线包含了一个显着的中断。在世界各地的许多地方，沉积岩的历史可以追溯到大约 5.4 亿年前的寒武纪，直接沉积在更古老的结晶岩上，包括已有超过 10 亿年历史的花岗岩。中间的地质层不存在，留下了被称为大不整合面的巨大记录。

paras.en: One of the clearest examples is visible in the Grand Canyon in the United States. This region was once part of Laurentia (modern North America), an ancient continental landmass. Similar gaps have been identified in Europe, Australia, Africa and Asia.
paras.zh: 最明显的例子之一是美国大峡谷。该地区曾经是古老大陆劳伦西亚（现代北美）的一部分。欧洲、澳大利亚、非洲和亚洲也存在类似的差距。

paras.en: The amount of missing time varies considerably between locations. In some places, approximately 200 million years of geological history are absent, while elsewhere the gap exceeds a billion years.
paras.zh: 不同地点的缺勤时间差别很大。在一些地方，大约没有2亿年的地质历史，而在其他地方，差距超过10亿年。

paras.en: How Forces Deep Inside Earth May Have Erased the Rock Record
paras.zh: 地球深处的力量如何抹掉岩石记录

paras.en: To investigate what caused these missing chapters, Dhungana worked with his supervisor and co-author, Associate Professor Nicolas Flament, to simulate the movement of Earth's mantle over hundreds of millions of years.
paras.zh: 为了调查导致这些缺失章节的原因，杜加纳与他的导师兼合著者尼古拉斯·弗拉门特副教授合作，模拟了地幔数亿年的运动。

paras.en: The mantle is an immense layer of hot, mostly solid rock beneath Earth's crust. Although this material appears rigid on human timescales, it can deform and flow extremely slowly over geological periods. Heat-driven circulation within the mantle, a process called mantle convection, can gradually raise enormous regions of Earth's surface or cause them to subside.
paras.zh: 地幔是地壳下一层巨大的炽热、大部分为固体的岩石。尽管这种材料在人类时间尺度上看起来是刚性的，但它可以在地质时期内变形并极其缓慢地流动。地幔内由热驱动的循环，这一过程称为地幔对流，可以逐渐抬升地球表面的大片区域或导致它们下沉。

paras.en: These vertical movements can influence whether ancient rocks are exposed to erosion or buried beneath new deposits. When a continent rises, wind, water and other natural processes can gradually wear away its surface. If the land later sinks, oceans can advance over it, allowing fresh sediment to accumulate on top of the eroded rock.
paras.zh: 这些垂直运动会影响古代岩石是否受到侵蚀或埋在新沉积物之下。当大陆上升时，风、水和其他自然过程会逐渐磨损其表面。如果陆地随后下沉，海洋就会淹没它，使新鲜的沉积物积聚在被侵蚀的岩石顶部。

paras.en: The researchers found that this process may explain both the disappearance of ancient rock layers and the preservation of the geological boundary that remains visible today.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，这一过程可以解释古代岩层的消失和至今仍可见的地质边界的保存。

paras.en: Ancient Continents Rose and Sank Over Millions of Years
paras.zh: 古代大陆数百万年来的崛起和沉没

paras.en: The simulations revealed a striking pattern across three major ancient continental regions: Laurentia, Baltica (northern Europe) and North China.
paras.zh: 模拟揭示了三个主要古代大陆地区的惊人模式：劳伦西亚、波罗的海（北欧）和华北。

paras.en: According to the models, mantle convection caused the ancient cores of these continents to rise during the Neoproterozoic Era, which extended from roughly one billion to 540 million years ago. This long interval preceded the Cambrian period, when animal life underwent a remarkable expansion in diversity, commonly known as the Cambrian explosion.
paras.zh: 根据模型，地幔对流导致这些大陆的古老核心在新元古代时期上升，这个时期从大约 10 亿年前延伸到 5.4 亿年前。这个漫长的时期发生在寒武纪之前，当时动物生命的多样性经历了显着的扩张，通常被称为寒武纪大爆发。

paras.en: As the continents remained elevated, prolonged erosion could have stripped away extensive layers of older rock, gradually removing hundreds of millions of years of geological history.
paras.zh: 由于大陆仍然处于升高状态，长期的侵蚀可能会剥去大面积的较古老的岩石，逐渐消除数亿年的地质历史。

paras.en: The researchers found that this period of uplift was followed by widespread subsidence during the Phanerozoic eon, which encompasses approximately the past 540 million years. As these ancient continental regions slowly sank, advancing seas covered their eroded surfaces. New sediments accumulated above the exposed older rocks, preserving the boundary between the two.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，这段抬升时期之后是显生宙期间的广泛下沉，这一时期大约涵盖了过去的 5.4 亿年。随着这些古老的大陆地区慢慢下沉，前进的海洋覆盖了它们被侵蚀的表面。新的沉积物堆积在暴露的旧岩石上方，保留了两者之间的边界。

paras.en: Over immense spans of time, this sequence of uplift, erosion, subsidence and sediment deposition could have produced the Great Unconformity seen in rock formations today.
paras.zh: 在漫长的时间跨度中，这一系列的隆起、侵蚀、沉降和沉积物沉积可能产生了今天岩层中所见的大不整合面。

paras.en: A New Explanation for One of Earth's Greatest Geological Mysteries
paras.zh: 对地球上最大的地质谜团之一的新解释

paras.en: A particularly important finding was how closely the computer simulations matched the geographical distribution of the Great Unconformity.
paras.zh: 一个特别重要的发现是计算机模拟与大不整合面的地理分布的吻合程度。

paras.en: The models predicted long-term uplift followed by subsidence in North America, northern Europe and North China, precisely the regions where the geological gap is especially well documented and preserved.
paras.zh: 这些模型预测了北美、北欧和华北地区的长期隆起和随后的沉降，而这些地区正是地质间隙得到特别详细记录和保存的地区。

paras.en: This agreement provides support for the idea that deep mantle movements played a major role in shaping the missing rock record. Rather than requiring a separate explanation for each location, the findings suggest that a common process operating deep within Earth may account for the widespread pattern.
paras.zh: 该协议支持了深部地幔运动在形成缺失的岩石记录方面发挥了重要作用的观点。研究结果表明，地球深处运行的一个共同过程可能解释了这种广泛的模式，而不是要求对每个位置进行单独的解释。

paras.en: "Sometimes what is missing can tell us more about the story of Earth than what we can see. A single, long period of uplift followed by a long period of sinking would have been the ideal recipe for removing the rock and preserving the worn surface," Associate Professor Flament said.
paras.zh: “有时候，缺失的东西可以告诉我们更多关于地球的故事，而不是我们所看到的。弗拉门特副教授说，一次长期的隆起，然后是长期的下沉，可能是去除岩石和保留磨损表面的理想方法。”

paras.en: The research offers a way to connect the geological evidence visible at Earth's surface with the slow processes occurring far below it. Although the findings do not establish that mantle convection was the only factor responsible for the Great Unconformity, they provide a testable explanation for why so much ancient geological history disappeared and how the remaining evidence survived.
paras.zh: 这项研究提供了一种将地球表面可见的地质证据与远低于地球的缓慢过程联系起来的方法。尽管这些发现并没有证明地幔对流是造成大不整合的唯一因素，但它们为为什么如此多的古代地质历史消失以及剩余的证据如何幸存提供了可检验的解释。

paras.en: "Many explanations for the Great Unconformity had been proposed but few had been tested against how the Earth actually behaves over time. It is a thrill to be able to propose a solution to this geological puzzle."
paras.zh: “人们对大不整合面提出了许多解释，但很少有人根据地球随时间的实际变化进行测试。能够为这个地质难题提出解决方案真是令人兴奋。”

paras.en: Materials provided by University of Wollongong. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由卧龙岗大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

paras.en: - Santosh Dhungana, Nicolas Flament. The deep Earth origin of the Great Unconformity. Nature, 2026; 659 (8139): 106 DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-11156-5
paras.zh: - 桑托什·杜加纳 (Santosh Dhungana)，尼古拉斯·弗拉门特 (Nicolas Flament)。大不整合面的地球深处起源。自然，2026； 659 (8139): 106 DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-11156-5

articles.title: A little-known protein could be a powerful weapon against Alzheimer’s

paras.en: A little-known protein could be a powerful weapon against Alzheimerâs
paras.zh: 一种鲜为人知的蛋白质可能是对抗阿尔茨海默病的有力武器

paras.en: - Scientists have uncovered a powerful natural defense against Alzheimerâs disease that could open the door to new treatments. By boosting a protein called SORLA, researchers significantly reduced toxic tau tangles, protected connections between brain cells, and prevented some of the brain shrinkage associated with neurodegeneration in mice. Removing the protein made the damage worse, highlighting its critical protective role.
paras.zh: - 科学家们发现了一种针对阿尔茨海默病的强大天然防御机制，这可能为新疗法打开大门。通过增强一种名为 SORLA 的蛋白质，研究人员显着减少了有毒的 tau 蛋白缠结，保护了脑细胞之间的连接，并防止了与小鼠神经退行性疾病相关的一些大脑萎缩。去除蛋白质会使损伤更加严重，凸显了其至关重要的保护作用。

paras.en: A protein that helps protect the brain may offer scientists a promising new way to fight Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia. Researchers have discovered that increasing levels of this protein can reduce the buildup of toxic tangles associated with brain damage, while also helping preserve the connections that allow nerve cells to communicate.
paras.zh: 一种有助于保护大脑的蛋白质可能为科学家提供一种有希望的新方法来对抗阿尔茨海默病和其他形式的痴呆症。研究人员发现，增加这种蛋白质的水平可以减少与脑损伤相关的有毒缠结的积累，同时还有助于保护神经细胞进行交流的连接。

paras.en: The findings, published in Science Advances by scientists at Sanford Burnham Prebys, suggest that strengthening the brain's own protective mechanisms could eventually lead to new treatments for neurodegenerative diseases. In experiments with mice, the researchers found that boosting the protein reduced several damaging changes associated with Alzheimer's, including brain shrinkage and the accumulation of abnormal tau proteins.
paras.zh: 桑福德伯纳姆普雷比学院的科学家在《科学进展》上发表的研究结果表明，加强大脑自身的保护机制最终可能会带来神经退行性疾病的新疗法。在小鼠实验中，研究人员发现，增加这种蛋白质的含量可以减少与阿尔茨海默氏症相关的几种破坏性变化，包括大脑萎缩和异常 tau 蛋白的积累。

paras.en: The discovery is particularly significant because tau plays an essential role in keeping healthy brain cells functioning. Under normal conditions, tau proteins help stabilize microtubules, tiny structures that provide internal support to neurons and help maintain the intricate networks of the nervous system.
paras.zh: 这一发现尤为重要，因为 tau 蛋白在保持健康脑细胞功能方面发挥着重要作用。在正常情况下，tau 蛋白有助于稳定微管，这种微小结构为神经元提供内部支持，并有助于维持神经系统的复杂网络。

paras.en: In Alzheimer's and several related disorders, however, tau proteins can become abnormal and stick together, forming harmful clumps known as tau tangles. These tangles disrupt the normal functioning of nerve cells and are associated with cognitive decline and neuronal death. Diseases characterized by abnormal tau accumulation are collectively called tauopathies.
paras.zh: 然而，在阿尔茨海默氏症和几种相关疾病中，tau 蛋白可能变得异常并粘在一起，形成称为 tau 缠结的有害团块。这些缠结会破坏神经细胞的正常功能，并与认知能力下降和神经元死亡有关。以 tau 蛋白异常积累为特征的疾病统称为 tau 病。

paras.en: A Protective Protein With a Surprising Role in Alzheimer's
paras.zh: 一种在阿尔茨海默病中具有惊人作用的保护性蛋白质

paras.en: The researchers investigated a protein called sorting-related receptor with A-type repeats (SORLA), which has already attracted scientific attention for its potential role in protecting the brain against Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 研究人员研究了一种名为 A 型重复分选相关受体 (SORLA) 的蛋白质，该蛋白质因其在保护大脑免受阿尔茨海默病的潜在作用而引起了科学界的关注。

paras.en: Previous studies have shown that SORLA can help limit the production and accumulation of amyloid-beta, another protein closely associated with Alzheimer's. Amyloid-beta can build up into plaques in the brain, making it one of the disease's major pathological hallmarks alongside tau tangles.
paras.zh: 先前的研究表明，SORLA 可以帮助限制β-淀粉样蛋白的产生和积累，β-淀粉样蛋白是另一种与阿尔茨海默病密切相关的蛋白质。 β 淀粉样蛋白可以在大脑中积聚成斑块，使其与 tau 蛋白缠结一起成为该疾病的主要病理特征之一。

paras.en: "In the last 15 or 20 years, considerable data has come out from our lab and other groups showing that SORLA can suppress one of the hallmarks of Alzheimer's disease -- amyloid-beta generation and accumulation," said Timothy Huang, PhD, assistant professor in the Center for Neurologic Diseases at Sanford Burnham Prebys.
paras.zh: “在过去的 15 或 20 年里，我们的实验室和其他小组得出的大量数据表明，SORLA 可以抑制阿尔茨海默病的标志之一——β-淀粉样蛋白的生成和积累，”桑福德伯纳姆普雷比学院神经系统疾病中心助理教授 Timothy Huang 博士说。

paras.en: "Very little was known, however, about whether SORLA affected the tau tangles reflected on the other side of the coin in Alzheimer's disease."
paras.zh: “然而，人们对 SORLA 是否影响阿尔茨海默病中硬币另一面的 tau 蛋白缠结影响知之甚少。”

paras.en: To investigate this question, the scientists developed a mouse model by breeding animals engineered to produce additional human SORLA with mice that develop tau tangles, brain atrophy, and cognitive impairments. This allowed them to examine whether higher SORLA levels could reduce tau accumulation and protect against the damage it causes.
paras.zh: 为了研究这个问题，科学家们开发了一种小鼠模型，将能够产生额外人类 SORLA 的动物与出现 tau 蛋白缠结、脑萎缩和认知障碍的小鼠进行繁殖。这使他们能够检查较高的 SORLA 水平是否可以减少 tau 积累并防止其造成的损害。

paras.en: Boosting SORLA Reduces Toxic Tau and Brain Shrinkage
paras.zh: 增强 SORLA 可减少有毒 Tau 蛋白和大脑萎缩

paras.en: The results revealed that additional SORLA provided protection against several processes that contribute to tau tangles and the progression of neurodegenerative disease.
paras.zh: 结果表明，额外的 SORLA 可以针对导致 tau 缠结和神经退行性疾病进展的多种过程提供保护。

paras.en: One important effect involved a process called hyperphosphorylation. This occurs when too many phosphate groups attach to tau proteins, altering their behavior and contributing to the development of harmful tangles. Higher SORLA levels reduced this abnormal modification.
paras.zh: 一个重要的影响涉及一种称为过度磷酸化的过程。当太多磷酸基团附着在 tau 蛋白上时，就会发生这种情况，改变它们的行为并导致有害缠结的发展。较高的 SORLA 水平减少了这种异常修饰。

paras.en: The protein also limited the ability of misfolded tau to act as "seeds" that encourage other tau proteins to clump together. This seeding process can help toxic tau aggregates multiply and spread their damaging effects.
paras.zh: 该蛋白还限制了错误折叠的 tau 蛋白作为“种子”的能力，从而鼓励其他 tau 蛋白聚集在一起。这种播种过程可以帮助有毒的 tau 蛋白聚集体繁殖并传播其破坏性影响。

paras.en: Beyond reducing tau abnormalities, SORLA helped preserve synapses, the specialized connections through which neurons communicate. It also protected synaptic plasticity, the brain's ability to strengthen or modify those connections, which is essential for learning, memory, and normal cognitive function.
paras.zh: 除了减少 tau 蛋白异常之外，SORLA 还有助于保护突触，即神经元进行交流的特殊连接。它还保护突触可塑性，即大脑加强或修改这些连接的能力，这对于学习、记忆和正常认知功能至关重要。

paras.en: "When you upregulate SORLA, you can suppress the negative effects found in tauopathies," said Huijie Huang, PhD, a staff scientist in the Huang lab at Sanford Burnham Prebys and lead author of the study.
paras.zh: “当你上调 SORLA 时，你可以抑制 tau蛋白病中发现的负面影响，”桑福德伯纳姆普雷比斯大学黄实验室的研究员、该研究的主要作者 Huijie Huang 博士说。

paras.en: "We found there was less brain atrophy and less tau accumulation, which was very exciting to see."
paras.zh: “我们发现脑萎缩和 tau 蛋白积累减少，这是非常令人兴奋的。”

paras.en: Removing the Protein Makes Brain Damage Worse
paras.zh: 去除蛋白质会使大脑损伤更加严重

paras.en: After observing the benefits of increasing SORLA, the researchers examined what would happen if the protein were missing entirely.
paras.zh: 在观察到增加 SORLA 的好处后，研究人员研究了如果该蛋白质完全缺失会发生什么。

paras.en: SORLA is produced using instructions encoded by a gene called Sorl1. Some people carry mutations that interfere with this gene's function, potentially disrupting the production or activity of the protective protein.
paras.zh: SORLA 是使用 Sorl1 基因编码的指令产生的。有些人携带的突变会干扰该基因的功能，可能会破坏保护性蛋白质的产生或活性。

paras.en: To investigate the consequences, the team studied genetically modified mice that lacked Sorl1 and therefore could not produce SORLA.
paras.zh: 为了研究其后果，研究小组研究了缺乏 Sorl1 并因此无法产生 SORLA 的转基因小鼠。

paras.en: The results contrasted sharply with those seen in mice carrying additional copies of the protein. Instead of protecting against tau-related damage, the absence of SORLA made the harmful effects more severe.
paras.zh: 结果与携带额外蛋白质拷贝的小鼠中观察到的结果形成鲜明对比。 SORLA 的缺失不但不能防止 tau 相关损伤，反而使有害影响更加严重。

paras.en: "The opposite turned out to be true when we deleted the ability to produce SORLA proteins," said Tim Huang, senior and corresponding author of the manuscript. "A lack of SORLA exacerbated the harmful effects observed in tauopathies."
paras.zh: 该手稿的资深通讯作者蒂姆·黄 (Tim Huang) 说：“当我们删除了产生 SORLA 蛋白的能力时，结果恰恰相反。” “缺乏 SORLA 会加剧在 tau 蛋白病中观察到的有害影响。”

paras.en: These contrasting results provided further evidence that SORLA plays an important protective role in the brain and may influence how severely tau-related diseases progress.
paras.zh: 这些对比结果进一步证明 SORLA 在大脑中发挥着重要的保护作用，并可能影响 tau 相关疾病进展的严重程度。

paras.en: A New Clue Could Lead to Alzheimer's Treatments
paras.zh: 一条新线索可能导致阿尔茨海默氏症的治疗
